You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/procurement-po (dev merged; procurement vendor master 6.1 done). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md Procurement (purchase requisitions = FULL, RFQs = FULL, purchase orders = FULL, approval/release strategies = PARTIAL "data-driven value-threshold rules only" — multi-characteristic/multi-step is the documented later); docs/architecture.md D-012 (these are NUMBERED documents with docflow predecessor/successor links: requisition→RFQ→PO chain), D-013 (idempotency on document-creating + approve/convert endpoints), D-014 (pagination/envelope), D-015 (MoneyType/QuantityType — PO line amounts), D-029 (opaque vendor/item ids via queries), D-022/D-025 (migrations/tests), D-007 (tenancy). Then read the EXACT patterns to mirror:
- backend/app/modules/procurement/ (the module you're extending): __init__.py, constants.py, models.py, schemas.py, service.py, queries.py, router.py
- backend/app/modules/finance/models/payables.py (header+lines document shape, DocumentMixin, status lifecycle DRAFT→POSTED, opaque partner_id + denormalized name + line tables) and finance/service/vendor_bills.py or journal.py (how a multi-line document is created/validated/numbered and how status transitions + docflow links are done)
- backend/app/modules/inventory/service/stock_moves.py (docflow linking + numbering on a document) 
- backend/app/modules/procurement/queries.py + finance/queries.py + inventory/queries.py (vendor_exists, vendor status, is_item_approved_for_vendor, item_exists, currency_exists — you validate against these)
- backend/app/core/{numbering.py, docflow.py, idempotency.py, pagination.py, models.py (mixins/money/qty), custom_fields.py if relevant, deps.py}
- backend/tests/modules/procurement/{factories.py, conftest.py}
Latest migration = 0024.

TASK — PLAN 6.2: requisition → RFQ → PO flow with data-driven approval threshold rules. Build the three procurement documents + the approval-rule engine:

1. `procurement/constants.py` additions:
   - Enums: RequisitionStatus (DRAFT|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|REJECTED|CONVERTED|CANCELLED), RfqStatus (DRAFT|SENT|QUOTED|CLOSED|CANCELLED), PurchaseOrderStatus (DRAFT|PENDING_APPROVAL|APPROVED|REJECTED|SENT|PARTIALLY_RECEIVED|RECEIVED|CLOSED|CANCELLED — note PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED are driven by 6.3 goods receipts; include them now as the lifecycle, but transitions INTO them happen in 6.3; document which are set here vs later). Keep ApprovalDecision (APPROVED|REJECTED).
   - Permissions: procurement.requisition.read/.manage/.approve, procurement.rfq.read/.manage, procurement.po.read/.manage/.approve, procurement.approval_rule.manage.
   - Number sequences: 'procurement.requisition' (PR-…), 'procurement.rfq' (RFQ-…), 'procurement.po' (PO-…) — claimed at document creation (D-012).
   - Doc types + docflow link types: requisition→rfq ("sourced_by"/"rfq_for"), rfq→po and requisition→po ("ordered_by"/"converted_to").
2. `procurement/models.py` → SPLIT into `models/` package now (it will exceed 400 lines with these documents): models/vendors.py (move the existing Vendor + VendorApprovedItem there), models/requisitions.py, models/rfqs.py, models/orders.py, models/approvals.py; models/__init__.py re-exports ALL (so `from app.modules.procurement.models import Vendor, PurchaseOrder` keeps working — update every import site). This is a behavior-preserving move; do it cleanly.
   - `PurchaseRequisition` (`proc_requisitions`) + `PurchaseRequisitionLine` (`proc_requisition_lines`): header UuidPKMixin/TenantMixin/AuditMixin/TimestampMixin/DocumentMixin; requisition_number (claimed at creation), status, requested_by (user id, nullable), needed_by_date (Date), notes; lines: line_number, item_id (opaque, validated via inventory/queries), description, quantity (QuantityType), uom_id (opaque), estimated_unit_cost (MoneyType nullable), currency_code. UNIQUE(tenant_id, requisition_id, line_number).
   - `Rfq` (`proc_rfqs`) + `RfqLine` (`proc_rfq_lines`): header with rfq_number, status, vendor_id (composite tenant_fk to proc_vendors — the vendor being asked to quote; an RFQ in v1 targets ONE vendor for simplicity, document; multi-bidder comparison is the parity later), currency_code, valid_until (Date nullable), source_requisition_id (nullable composite tenant_fk); lines: line_number, item_id, description, quantity, uom_id, quoted_unit_cost (MoneyType nullable — filled when the vendor quotes). UNIQUE(tenant_id, rfq_id, line_number).
   - `PurchaseOrder` (`proc_purchase_orders`) + `PurchaseOrderLine` (`proc_purchase_order_lines`): header with po_number, status, vendor_id (composite tenant_fk), currency_code, order_date (Date), expected_date (Date nullable), payment_terms_days (snapshot from vendor at creation), total_amount (MoneyType — sum of line nets, maintained), notes, approval fields (approved_by user id nullable, approved_at nullable), source_requisition_id + source_rfq_id (nullable composite fks); lines: line_number, item_id (opaque), description, quantity (QuantityType ordered), uom_id, unit_cost (MoneyType), line_amount (MoneyType = qty×unit_cost), received_quantity (QuantityType default 0 — updated by 6.3 GR; include the column now), tax_code_id (opaque finance tax code, nullable — for the bill in 6.4). UNIQUE(tenant_id, po_id, line_number). Indexes per PERFORMANCE §1: (tenant_id, status), (tenant_id, vendor_id, status).
   - `ApprovalRule` (`proc_approval_rules`): UuidPKMixin/TenantMixin/AuditMixin/TimestampMixin; document_type (REQUISITION|PURCHASE_ORDER — which doc the rule governs), threshold_amount (MoneyType — orders/requisitions at or above this need approval), currency_code, is_active, description. The DATA-DRIVEN rule: a PO/PR whose total ≥ the active threshold for its document_type requires approval before it can be SENT/CONVERTED; below threshold auto-approves. Keep it a single-characteristic (amount) rule per parity; multi-characteristic/multi-step is the later. UNIQUE/index (tenant_id, document_type).
3. `procurement/schemas.py` (split into schemas/ or sibling files if >400): Create/Update/Read/Filter for requisition (+lines), rfq (+lines), PO (+lines), approval rule. Plus action payloads: SubmitRequisition, ApproveDecision (approve/reject + comment), ConvertRequisitionToRfq, ConvertRfqToPo / ConvertRequisitionToPo, RecordQuote (rfq line quotes).
4. `procurement/service/` (package — split per document: service/requisitions.py, service/rfqs.py, service/orders.py, service/approvals.py, service/conversions.py + service/__init__.py re-export; each <400 lines):
   - Requisition: create (DRAFT, claim PR number, validate items exist + qty>0), submit (DRAFT→SUBMITTED; evaluate approval rule for document_type REQUISITION on the estimated total → if ≥ threshold status stays SUBMITTED awaiting approve; else auto APPROVED), approve/reject (SUBMITTED→APPROVED/REJECTED, permission procurement.requisition.approve), update/cancel (DRAFT only / not-converted).
   - RFQ: create from scratch OR from an approved requisition (convert: copy lines, link docflow requisition→rfq, set source_requisition_id), send (DRAFT→SENT), record_quote (fill quoted_unit_cost per line; SENT→QUOTED), close.
   - PO: create from scratch / from an approved requisition / from a quoted RFQ (convert: copy lines with unit_cost from the RFQ quote or requisition estimate, snapshot vendor payment terms + currency, link docflow, set source ids); validate vendor is ACTIVE (not BLOCKED/INACTIVE — via procurement/queries vendor status) and every line item is APPROVED for that vendor (is_item_approved_for_vendor — or allow non-approved with a soft policy? ENFORCE approved-items: a PO line item must be in the vendor's approved list, else 422 procurement.item_not_approved; document this is the v1 source-control rule). Compute line_amount + total_amount. submit_for_approval/auto-approve: on attempting to SEND a PO, evaluate the PURCHASE_ORDER approval rule on total_amount → ≥ threshold ⇒ PENDING_APPROVAL (requires procurement.po.approve to approve→APPROVED), below ⇒ auto APPROVED; only APPROVED POs can be SENT. approve/reject. cancel (not if received). 
   - Approval rules: CRUD; the evaluation helper `requires_approval(document_type, amount, currency) -> bool` reading the active rule (no active rule ⇒ no approval needed; document). 
   - Idempotency on create + convert + approve endpoints (D-013).
   - Numbering claimed at creation (these documents are permanent on create — DRAFT requisitions still get a PR number, matching how the chain is referenced; OR claim at submit? Mirror finance: finance claims at POSTING. For procurement, claim at CREATION so the document is referenceable immediately — document the choice; gaplessness still holds because creation is the committing transaction).
5. `procurement/queries.py` additions: `get_purchase_order(po_id)`, `po_line_open_quantity(po_line_id)` (ordered - received — used by 6.3 GR + 6.4 match), `get_po_for_receipt(po_id)` (the data GR needs: lines, items, expected qty, accounts), `open_po_lines_for_vendor`. Keep it the only imported file.
6. `procurement/router.py` (or split into requisition_router/rfq_router/po_router siblings mounted into router.py — the finance journal_router/ap_router precedent — to stay under 400 lines): full REST for the three documents + actions (submit, approve, reject, convert, record-quote, send) + approval-rule CRUD. Permission-guard each (manage vs approve distinct). Paginated lists with filters (status, vendor, date). PERFORMANCE §6. Mount.
7. `procurement/events.py`: define events the chain publishes IF any cross-module effect happens now. In 6.2 NOTHING posts to finance/inventory yet (GR is 6.3, bill is 6.4) — so NO events.py yet unless a PO approval should notify. Skip it; 6.3 introduces the first procurement event (goods receipt → inventory move). Document.
8. Migration `0025_procurement_documents.py` (down_revision 0024): all the new proc_ tables + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters. (The models/ package split is a code move, not a schema change — table names unchanged for Vendor/VendorApprovedItem.)
9. `docs/modules/procurement.md`: extend with the requisition→RFQ→PO chain, the approval-threshold rule model, the approved-items source-control rule, status lifecycles, what 6.3/6.4 add. 
10. Tests `backend/tests/modules/procurement/`: extend factories (build_requisition/build_rfq/build_po/build_approval_rule). New test files: test_requisitions.py (CRUD, submit, approval-rule gating: above-threshold needs approve, below auto-approves; approve/reject; RBAC on approve), test_rfqs.py (create, convert-from-requisition with docflow link, record quote, send), test_purchase_orders.py (create from scratch/requisition/rfq with docflow + source ids + line amounts + total; vendor-must-be-active; item-must-be-approved-for-vendor → 422; approval gating on send; approve→send), test_approval_rules.py (threshold evaluation incl. no-rule case + currency), test_procurement_api.py (endpoints, RBAC manage vs approve, pagination, ≤3 budgets, idempotency on create/convert/approve, tenant isolation, docflow chain endpoint shows requisition→rfq→po). Query-counter on the list endpoints + a bound on convert (no N+1 over lines beyond copying them).

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema at the pg url, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; EVERY file <400 lines (the models/ + service/ + maybe router/ + schemas/ splits are REQUIRED — do them from the start, don't write a 600-line file then split); comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 6.2 + any DECISIONS.md entry for consequential choices (e.g. D-040 approval-rule model / numbering-at-creation / approved-items enforcement). Run the STRUCTURE §9 self-check and report it.

Return: files created/changed (note the models/ package move + every import site updated), the document chain + status lifecycles, the approval-rule evaluation rule, the approved-items enforcement decision, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, and deviations with one-line justification.

1	"""Procurement constants (STRUCTURE §3): the vendor-master enums and the permission keys,
2	registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line
5	cap, the finance precedent); PLAN 6.1 sits well under that.
6	
7	**Payment-terms modeling (decided here).** A vendor carries ``payment_terms_days`` — a plain
8	integer net-days value (30 = NET30) — NOT a separate terms master/value-set. This matches how AP
9	already computes a bill's due date (bill_date + net days) and keeps v1 simple; richer term
10	schedules (e.g. 2/10 NET30 early-payment discounts, multi-instalment plans) are deferred per the
11	parity doc and would arrive as a terms entity referenced from the vendor. The field is stored with
12	a CHECK >= 0 on the vendor.
13	
14	**Vendor codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant** (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, vendor_code)`` on
15	proc_vendors) — mirroring inventory ``item_code`` and the finance account ``code``: a vendor MASTER
16	carries no gapless document number (a code, not a number). The P2P DOCUMENTS in 6.2+ (requisitions,
17	POs, GRs) DO claim gapless numbers — a posted document in the D-012 sense — but the master does not.
18	"""
19	
20	from enum import StrEnum
21	
22	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
23	
24	
25	class VendorStatus(StrEnum):
26	    """A vendor's lifecycle / usability state (parity: vendor master block levels).
27	
28	    - ACTIVE: usable — new purchase orders may name this vendor (the only state 6.2+ accepts).
29	    - BLOCKED: temporarily barred — kept for history and existing open documents, but the P2P
30	      chain (6.2) refuses to raise a NEW PO against it (a soft block; the vendor can be unblocked
31	      back to ACTIVE).
32	    - INACTIVE: retired — no new business, retained for reporting and existing AP history.
33	
34	    Transitions are unrestricted between the three (ACTIVE↔BLOCKED↔INACTIVE all allowed): a block
35	    is reversible and a retired vendor can be reactivated. The only rule the service enforces is
36	    that the target is a valid VendorStatus; no terminal state, because vendor history must stay
37	    referenceable and a mistaken retire/block must be undoable (the append-only ledger lives in
38	    finance AP, not here)."""
39	
40	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
41	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
42	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
43	
44	
45	# The default net-days a vendor is created with when the payload omits it (NET30 — the common
46	# commercial default; AP's due-date math is bill_date + this many days). Stored on the vendor.
47	DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30
48	
49	
50	# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
51	# Two keys: read the vendor master (+ its approved items) vs create/edit it. Approved-item
52	# management is a vendor-master edit, so it rides VENDOR_MANAGE rather than a third key — adding an
53	# approved item is configuring the vendor, not a distinct privileged action (the inventory
54	# item/uom-conversion precedent: nested config shares the parent's manage key).
55	PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ = "procurement.vendor.read"
56	PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE = "procurement.vendor.manage"
57	
58	register_permissions(
59	    PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ,
60	    PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE,
61	    descriptions={
62	        PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ: "Read vendors and their approved items",
63	        PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE: "Create and edit vendors and their approved items",
64	    },
65	)
66

1	"""Procurement vendor master (PLAN 6.1): the ``Vendor`` entity and the v1 "approved items"
2	info-record-lite (``VendorApprovedItem``).
3	
4	ONE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a models/ package only at the 400-line cap, the inventory
5	precedent); two tables fit well under it.
6	
7	Design decisions baked in here:
8	
9	- **The vendor's id IS finance AP's opaque ``partner_id`` (D-029).** Finance owns no vendor table;
10	  every AP bill/payment carries an opaque ``partner_id`` (no FK) + a denormalized ``partner_name``.
11	  That id is exactly this ``Vendor.id``. Procurement is ABOVE finance in the dependency order, so
12	  finance can never FK to this table; the link is by opaque id only, resolved through
13	  ``procurement/queries.get_vendor_for_partner``.
14	
15	- **``payment_terms_days`` is a plain net-days integer on the vendor**, not a terms master — it
16	  drives AP due dates (bill_date + days), the simplest model that matches how AP already computes
17	  them (constants.py documents the deferral of richer term schedules). A DB CHECK keeps it >= 0.
18	
19	- **``VendorApprovedItem.item_id`` is an OPAQUE inventory item id (D-029)** — a plain ``sa.Uuid``
20	  column, NOT a ``tenant_fk`` to ``inv_items``: procurement may READ inventory via
21	  ``inventory/queries.item_exists`` (validated in the service) but never cross-module FK-references
22	  it. Contrast the vendor link on the same table, which IS a composite ``tenant_fk`` to
23	  ``proc_vendors`` (an intra-module parent). This is the info-record-lite: the vendor↔item link
24	  with the vendor's own SKU, but NO price / lead-time / valid-from-to (deferred per parity).
25	
26	Both tables follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop: ``tenant_unique()`` on every table a
27	child references, ``tenant_fk()`` composites for every INTRA-module cross-row link. Enum-valued
28	columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value (the core/finance/inventory
29	convention, no ``sa.Enum``); the service maps to/from the constants classes.
30	"""
31	
32	import uuid
33	
34	import sqlalchemy as sa
35	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
36	
37	from app.core.models import (
38	    AuditMixin,
39	    Base,
40	    TenantMixin,
41	    TimestampMixin,
42	    UuidPKMixin,
43	    tenant_fk,
44	    tenant_unique,
45	)
46	from app.modules.procurement.constants import DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS, VendorStatus
47	
48	
49	class Vendor(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
50	    """A vendor / supplier master record (parity: supplier master — FULL in v1).
51	
52	    ``vendor_code`` is user-supplied and unique per tenant (no auto-numbering — the account-code /
53	    item-code precedent). ``status`` gates new POs in 6.2 (BLOCKED/INACTIVE vendors cannot receive
54	    them). ``default_currency_code`` defaults onto a vendor's bills/POs and is validated to exist in
55	    finance's currency catalog (D-029, via ``finance/queries.currency_exists``).
56	    ``payment_terms_days`` is the net-days value AP adds to a bill date for the due date (CHECK >=
57	    0). Contact fields are kept modest (email/phone + a single address line). The row's ``id`` IS
58	    the opaque ``partner_id`` finance AP stores (D-029). Audited (D-010): master data driving where
59	    money is owed."""
60	
61	    __tablename__ = "proc_vendors"
62	    __table_args__ = (
63	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
64	            "tenant_id", "vendor_code", name="uq_proc_vendors_tenant_id_vendor_code"
65	        ),
66	        tenant_unique(),
67	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
68	        sa.CheckConstraint(
69	            "payment_terms_days >= 0", name="ck_proc_vendors_payment_terms_days_non_negative"
70	        ),
71	        # The vendor list filters on (tenant_id, status) and sorts by vendor_code (PERFORMANCE §1):
72	        # composite so the filtered + paginated reference list is index-served.
73	        sa.Index("ix_proc_vendors_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
74	    )
75	
76	    vendor_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
77	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
78	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
79	        sa.String(20),
80	        nullable=False,
81	        default=VendorStatus.ACTIVE.value,
82	        server_default="ACTIVE",
83	    )
84	    default_currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
85	    payment_terms_days: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
86	        sa.Integer,
87	        nullable=False,
88	        default=DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS,
89	        server_default=str(DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS),
90	    )
91	    # The vendor's tax/VAT registration reference (free text, optional).
92	    tax_reference: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
93	    email: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(320), nullable=True)
94	    phone: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)
95	    address: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
96	    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
97	
98	
99	class VendorApprovedItem(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
100	    """An approved (vendor, item) link — the v1 info-record-lite (parity: purchasing info records,
101	    PARTIAL).
102	
103	    Records that a vendor is an approved source for an inventory item, optionally with the vendor's
104	    own SKU (``vendor_item_code``). ``vendor_id`` is a composite ``tenant_fk`` to ``proc_vendors``
105	    (an intra-module parent). ``item_id`` is an OPAQUE inventory item id (D-029): a plain
106	    ``sa.Uuid``, NOT an FK — the service validates it exists via ``inventory/queries.item_exists``.
107	    ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, vendor_id, item_id)`` so a vendor approves an item at most once.
108	    Deliberately NO price / lead-time / valid-from-to: those time-dependent conditions are deferred
109	    per the parity doc and would extend this table later.
110	
111	    NOT AuditMixin: an approved-item link is low-churn config that rides the vendor's audit story
112	    (it has no independent lifecycle), keeping the audit log lean — the same reasoning inventory's
113	    ``UomConversion`` applies to the per-item conversion rows."""
114	
115	    __tablename__ = "proc_vendor_approved_items"
116	    __table_args__ = (
117	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
118	            "tenant_id",
119	            "vendor_id",
120	            "item_id",
121	            name="uq_proc_vendor_approved_items_tenant_id_vendor_id_item_id",
122	        ),
123	        tenant_unique(),
124	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
125	        tenant_fk("proc_vendors", "vendor_id"),
126	        # FK index for "this vendor's approved items" — the nested list endpoint's read path.
127	        sa.Index(
128	            "ix_proc_vendor_approved_items_tenant_id_vendor_id", "tenant_id", "vendor_id"
129	        ),
130	    )
131	
132	    vendor_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
133	    # Opaque inventory item id (D-029): no cross-module FK; validated via inventory/queries.
134	    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
135	    vendor_item_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
136	    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
137	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
138	    )

1	"""Procurement request/response schemas (Pydantic v2, ApiModel base) for PLAN 6.1.
2	
3	Read schemas mirror the models field-for-field in snake_case; ``status`` is typed with the
4	``VendorStatus`` constant (ApiModel's ``use_enum_values`` serializes it as its UPPER_SNAKE string,
5	matching the column). The vendor master carries no money/quantity fields — everything here is a
6	scalar (codes, names, an int net-days, contact strings) — so no Decimal-as-string handling is
7	needed (D-015 applies only where money/qty appears, which is the P2P documents in 6.2+).
8	
9	Create/Update carry only client-settable fields; ids, timestamps and tenant_id are server-owned.
10	``payment_terms_days`` is OPTIONAL on create (defaulted to NET30 by the service when omitted);
11	``vendor_code`` is immutable after creation (AP partner_id history and later POs reference the
12	vendor) so it is absent from VendorUpdate.
13	"""

16	from datetime import datetime
17	
18	from pydantic import Field
19	
20	from app.core.schemas import ApiModel
21	from app.modules.procurement.constants import DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS, VendorStatus

28	    ``default_currency_code`` must exist in finance's currency catalog (validated, D-029).
29	    ``payment_terms_days`` defaults to NET30 when omitted and must be >= 0. ``status`` defaults
30	    to ACTIVE."""

32	    vendor_code: str
33	    name: str
34	    default_currency_code: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=3)
35	    status: VendorStatus = VendorStatus.ACTIVE
36	    payment_terms_days: int = Field(default=DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS, ge=0)
37	    tax_reference: str | None = None

39	    phone: str | None = None
40	    address: str | None = None

48	    stay >= 0; ``status`` may move freely between ACTIVE/BLOCKED/INACTIVE."""

51	    default_currency_code: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=3, max_length=3)

1	"""Procurement vendor-master business logic (PLAN 6.1): vendor CRUD + approved-item management.
2	
3	The service layer owns every rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7); the router stays thin. Rules enforced here:
4	
5	- ``vendor_code`` uniqueness per tenant (friendly ConflictError before the DB UNIQUE would raise);
6	- ``default_currency_code`` must exist in finance's currency catalog (D-029, via
7	  ``finance/queries.currency_exists`` — never a cross-module FK);
8	- ``payment_terms_days`` >= 0 (schema bounds it too; the DB CHECK is the backstop);
9	- ``status`` transitions are UNRESTRICTED between ACTIVE/BLOCKED/INACTIVE (constants.VendorStatus
10	  documents why — a block/retire must be reversible; the P2P chain in 6.2 reads the status to refuse
11	  POs against non-ACTIVE vendors, but the master itself imposes no terminal state);
12	- approved items: the ``item_id`` must exist in inventory (D-029, via
13	  ``inventory/queries.item_exists``); a vendor cannot approve the same item twice (friendly
14	  ConflictError before the UNIQUE backstop).
15	
16	ONE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a service/ package only at the 400-line cap, the finance /
17	inventory precedent); both aggregates fit well under it. ``from __future__ import annotations``
18	keeps ``Page[Vendor]`` (the ORM model) a string at import; the router re-validates page items.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import uuid
24	
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
27	
28	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
29	from app.core.pagination import (
30	    DEFAULT_LIMIT,
31	    OrderKey,
32	    SortDirection,
33	    filter_fingerprint,
34	    paginate,
35	)
36	from app.core.schemas import Page
37	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
38	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
39	from app.modules.procurement.constants import VendorStatus
40	from app.modules.procurement.models import Vendor, VendorApprovedItem
41	from app.modules.procurement.schemas import (
42	    VendorApprovedItemCreate,
43	    VendorCreate,
44	    VendorFilter,
45	    VendorUpdate,
46	)
47	
48	# --- Vendors ------------------------------------------------------------------
49	
50	
51	async def _vendor_by_code(
52	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_code: str
53	) -> Vendor | None:
54	    stmt = select(Vendor).where(
55	        Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.vendor_code == vendor_code
56	    )
57	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
58	
59	
60	async def _validate_currency(
61	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, currency_code: str
62	) -> None:
63	    """The vendor's default currency must exist in finance's catalog (D-029): validated through the
64	    finance queries contract, never a cross-module FK."""
65	    if not await finance_queries.currency_exists(session, tenant_id, currency_code):
66	        raise ValidationFailedError(
67	            message=f"Currency {currency_code} does not exist in the finance catalog",
68	            code="procurement.currency_not_found",
69	            details={"currency_code": currency_code},
70	        )
71	
72	
73	async def get_vendor(
74	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
75	) -> Vendor:
76	    vendor = await session.get(Vendor, vendor_id)
77	    if vendor is None or vendor.tenant_id != tenant_id:
78	        raise NotFoundError(message="Vendor not found", code="procurement.vendor_not_found")
79	    return vendor
80	
81	
82	async def create_vendor(
83	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: VendorCreate
84	) -> Vendor:
85	    """Create a vendor. Rejects a duplicate vendor_code; validates the default currency exists in
86	    finance. ``status`` defaults to ACTIVE; ``payment_terms_days`` defaults to NET30 (schema)."""
87	    if await _vendor_by_code(session, tenant_id, payload.vendor_code) is not None:
88	        raise ConflictError(
89	            message=f"A vendor with code {payload.vendor_code} already exists",
90	            code="procurement.vendor_code_conflict",
91	            details={"vendor_code": payload.vendor_code},
92	        )
93	    await _validate_currency(session, tenant_id, payload.default_currency_code)
94	    vendor = Vendor(
95	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
96	        vendor_code=payload.vendor_code,
97	        name=payload.name,
98	        status=VendorStatus(payload.status).value,
99	        default_currency_code=payload.default_currency_code,
100	        payment_terms_days=payload.payment_terms_days,
101	        tax_reference=payload.tax_reference,
102	        email=payload.email,
103	        phone=payload.phone,
104	        address=payload.address,
105	        notes=payload.notes,
106	    )
107	    session.add(vendor)
108	    await session.flush()
109	    return vendor
110	
111	
112	async def update_vendor(
113	    session: AsyncSession,
114	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
115	    vendor_id: uuid.UUID,
116	    payload: VendorUpdate,
117	) -> Vendor:
118	    """Partial update of a vendor (D-010: mutate the loaded object so the audit diff is captured).
119	    ``vendor_code`` is immutable and absent from the schema; a changed ``default_currency_code`` is
120	    re-validated against finance; ``status`` may move freely between the three states."""
121	    vendor = await get_vendor(session, tenant_id, vendor_id)
122	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
123	    if data.get("default_currency_code") is not None:
124	        await _validate_currency(session, tenant_id, data["default_currency_code"])
125	    if data.get("status") is not None:
126	        data["status"] = VendorStatus(data["status"]).value
127	    for field, value in data.items():
128	        setattr(vendor, field, value)
129	    await session.flush()
130	    return vendor
131	
132	
133	async def list_vendors(
134	    session: AsyncSession,
135	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
136	    *,
137	    filters: VendorFilter,
138	    cursor: str | None = None,
139	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
140	) -> Page[Vendor]:
141	    """Keyset-paginated vendor list ordered by vendor_code (D-014). The optional status filter
142	    narrows the set and folds into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor cannot bleed across views
143	    (the (tenant_id, status) index serves the filtered page, PERFORMANCE §1)."""
144	    stmt = select(Vendor).where(Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id)
145	    if filters.status is not None:
146	        stmt = stmt.where(Vendor.status == VendorStatus(filters.status).value)
147	    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(filters.status)
148	    return await paginate(
149	        session,
150	        stmt,
151	        order_by=[OrderKey(Vendor.vendor_code, SortDirection.ASC)],
152	        pk=Vendor.id,
153	        cursor=cursor,
154	        limit=limit,
155	        filters=fingerprint,
156	    )
157	
158	
159	# --- Approved items (the v1 info-record-lite) ---------------------------------
160	
161	
162	async def list_approved_items(
163	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
164	) -> list[VendorApprovedItem]:
165	    """The vendor's approved items, ordered by creation (PLAN 6.1). 404s if the vendor does not
166	    exist (so a missing vendor and an empty list are distinguishable)."""
167	    await get_vendor(session, tenant_id, vendor_id)
168	    stmt = (
169	        select(VendorApprovedItem)
170	        .where(
171	            VendorApprovedItem.tenant_id == tenant_id,
172	            VendorApprovedItem.vendor_id == vendor_id,
173	        )
174	        .order_by(VendorApprovedItem.created_at, VendorApprovedItem.id)
175	    )
176	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
177	
178	
179	async def add_approved_item(
180	    session: AsyncSession,
181	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
182	    vendor_id: uuid.UUID,
183	    payload: VendorApprovedItemCreate,
184	) -> VendorApprovedItem:
185	    """Approve an inventory item for a vendor (info-record-lite). Validates the vendor exists, the
186	    item exists in inventory (D-029, via ``inventory/queries.item_exists`` — no cross-module FK),
187	    and the (vendor, item) pair is not already approved (friendly ConflictError before the UNIQUE
188	    backstop)."""
189	    await get_vendor(session, tenant_id, vendor_id)
190	    if not await inventory_queries.item_exists(session, tenant_id, payload.item_id):
191	        raise ValidationFailedError(
192	            message="Referenced inventory item does not exist",
193	            code="procurement.item_not_found",
194	            details={"item_id": str(payload.item_id)},
195	        )
196	    existing = (
197	        await session.execute(
198	            select(VendorApprovedItem.id).where(
199	                VendorApprovedItem.tenant_id == tenant_id,
200	                VendorApprovedItem.vendor_id == vendor_id,
201	                VendorApprovedItem.item_id == payload.item_id,
202	            )
203	        )
204	    ).first()
205	    if existing is not None:
206	        raise ConflictError(
207	            message="This item is already approved for the vendor",
208	            code="procurement.approved_item_conflict",
209	            details={"vendor_id": str(vendor_id), "item_id": str(payload.item_id)},
210	        )
211	    approved = VendorApprovedItem(
212	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
213	        vendor_id=vendor_id,
214	        item_id=payload.item_id,
215	        vendor_item_code=payload.vendor_item_code,
216	        is_active=payload.is_active,
217	    )
218	    session.add(approved)
219	    await session.flush()
220	    return approved
221	
222	
223	async def remove_approved_item(
224	    session: AsyncSession,
225	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
226	    vendor_id: uuid.UUID,
227	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
228	) -> None:
229	    """Un-approve an item for a vendor (PLAN 6.1). 404s if the (vendor, item) approval does not
230	    exist. A hard delete: the approved-item link is low-churn config with no document history of its
231	    own (unlike a posted document), so removal is a real delete, not a status flip."""
232	    stmt = select(VendorApprovedItem).where(
233	        VendorApprovedItem.tenant_id == tenant_id,
234	        VendorApprovedItem.vendor_id == vendor_id,
235	        VendorApprovedItem.item_id == item_id,
236	    )
237	    approved = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
238	    if approved is None:
239	        raise NotFoundError(
240	            message="Approved item not found",
241	            code="procurement.approved_item_not_found",
242	        )
243	    await session.delete(approved)
244	    await session.flush()

1	"""Procurement's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Procurement sits above inventory (and finance) in the dependency order: the P2P documents in
4	6.2–6.4 (requisition → RFQ → PO → goods receipt → 3-way match) and finance AP reporting read THIS
5	file to resolve vendor state synchronously; procurement imports finance/queries + inventory/queries
6	downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is the ONLY procurement file
7	other modules import.
8	
9	The central D-029 link: finance AP stores a vendor on each bill/payment as an opaque ``partner_id``
10	(no FK). ``get_vendor_for_partner`` resolves that ``partner_id`` back to a ``Vendor`` so AP aging /
11	reporting can render the vendor's name and payment terms — the ``partner_id`` IS the ``Vendor.id``,
12	so it is a thin alias over ``get_vendor`` named for the reporting intent.
13	
14	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
15	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
16	"""
17	
18	import uuid
19

21	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

28	) -> Vendor | None:
29	    """The vendor with ``vendor_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets another module read a vendor's
30	    master fields (name, status, default currency, payment terms) without importing procurement
31	    models directly — the analogue of inventory's ``get_item``."""
32	    stmt = select(Vendor).where(Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.id == vendor_id)
33	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

40	    reporting calls this to resolve a bill's ``partner_id`` to a vendor name + payment terms. The

42	    named for the reporting intent — kept as its own function so AP call sites read intent-first and

1	"""Procurement HTTP layer (thin): parse -> call service -> return schema (PLAN 6.1).
2	
3	REST under ``/api/v1/procurement``: vendors (CRUD + filtered paginated list) and the per-vendor
4	approved-items nested resource (GET/POST the collection, DELETE one by item id). Every route is
5	guarded by a procurement permission key (D-009). Writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so
6	audit rows ride the same transaction; results are validated into their Read schema AFTER the uow
7	commits.
8	
9	The vendor list is slow-changing reference data, so it supports conditional GETs via a tenant-scoped
10	collection ETag (PERFORMANCE §3 / D-035): an If-None-Match hit returns 304 without running the page
11	query. The status filter folds into the request fingerprint so a filtered 304 is correct.
12	"""
13	
14	import uuid
15	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
16	
17	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
18	
19	from app.core.conditional import collection_etag, conditional_response, request_fingerprint
20	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
21	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
22	from app.core.pagination import CursorParams, cursor_params, map_page
23	from app.core.rbac import require_permission
24	from app.core.schemas import Page
25	from app.modules.procurement import service
26	from app.modules.procurement.constants import (
27	    PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE,
28	    PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ,
29	)
30	from app.modules.procurement.models import Vendor
31	from app.modules.procurement.schemas import (
32	    VendorApprovedItemCreate,
33	    VendorApprovedItemRead,
34	    VendorCreate,
35	    VendorFilter,
36	    VendorRead,
37	    VendorUpdate,
38	)
39	
40	router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/procurement", tags=["procurement"])
41	CursorParamsDep = Depends(cursor_params)
42	
43	
44	async def _commit[T](session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
45	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow, returning its ORM result refreshed in the async
46	    context so a sync ``model_validate`` never trips MissingGreenlet (twin of inventory _commit)."""
47	    holder: list[T] = []
48	
49	    async def _work() -> None:
50	        result = await work()
51	        await session.refresh(result)
52	        holder.append(result)
53	
54	    await run_in_uow(session, _work)
55	    return holder[0]
56	
57	
58	# --- Vendors ------------------------------------------------------------------
59	
60	
61	@router.get(
62	    "/vendors",
63	    response_model=Page[VendorRead],
64	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ))],
65	)
66	async def list_vendors(
67	    request: Request,
68	    response: Response,
69	    current: CurrentUserDep,
70	    session: SessionDep,
71	    params: CursorParams = CursorParamsDep,
72	    status: str | None = None,
73	) -> Page[VendorRead] | Response:
74	    """Conditional-GET supported (D-035): collection ETag over the vendor reference list; the
75	    status filter folds into the request fingerprint so a filtered 304 is correct."""
76	    filters = VendorFilter(status=status)
77	    fingerprint = request_fingerprint(params.cursor, params.limit, status)
78	    etag = await collection_etag(session, Vendor, request_fingerprint=fingerprint)
79	
80	    async def builder() -> Page[VendorRead]:
81	        page = await service.list_vendors(
82	            session, current.tenant_id, filters=filters, cursor=params.cursor, limit=params.limit
83	        )
84	        return map_page(page, VendorRead)
85	
86	    return await conditional_response(request, response, etag, builder)
87

90	    "/vendors",
91	    response_model=VendorRead,
92	    status_code=201,
93	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE))],
94	)

97	) -> VendorRead:

100	    )

108	)

113	    return VendorRead.model_validate(vendor)

135

1	"""Accounts Payable: vendor bills, payments and payment allocations (PLAN 4.5, D-029).
2	
3	The AP sub-ledger is keyed by an OPAQUE ``partner_id`` (D-029): finance is the bottom of the
4	dependency order, so it never FK-references a vendor master (that lives in procurement, above
5	finance). Each AP document carries the opaque ``partner_id`` plus a denormalized ``partner_name``
6	for display; the owning module guarantees the id. Open items (the amount still owed on a bill)
7	live in ``open_amount`` on the bill, reduced as payments allocate against it.
8	
9	Every AP document posts through the universal journal (D-017): a ``VendorBill`` registers in
10	core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin) and gets a ``journal_entry_id`` + system number at
11	posting; a ``VendorPayment`` is created and posted in one step, clearing the open items its
12	allocations name. Realized FX at clearing (D-019) is computed in the SERVICE, posted inside the
13	payment journal entry — no extra columns here.
14	
15	Fifth file in the finance ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3); re-exported from ``models/__init__``.
16	Money columns use ``MoneyType`` (D-015, exact on both engines). All cross-row links are composite
17	tenant FKs (D-007 backstop) EXCEPT ``partner_id`` (opaque, no FK — D-029) and the dimension ids.
18	Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum value, as elsewhere in finance.
19	"""
20	
21	import uuid
22	from datetime import date
23	
24	import sqlalchemy as sa
25	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
26	
27	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
28	from app.core.models import (
29	    AuditMixin,
30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,
32	    TimestampMixin,
33	    UuidPKMixin,
34	    tenant_fk,
35	    tenant_unique,
36	)
37	from app.core.money import MoneyType
38	from app.modules.finance.constants import BillStatus, PaymentStatus
39	
40	
41	class VendorBill(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
42	    """A vendor bill / supplier invoice (PLAN 4.5). Registered in core_documents at creation
43	    (DocumentMixin, doc_number NULL); the gapless system ``bill_number`` is claimed at POSTING
44	    (D-012). ``partner_id`` is the OPAQUE vendor id (D-029 — no FK); ``partner_name`` is the
45	    denormalized display name. ``bill_external_ref`` is the vendor's own document number (free
46	    text, not unique). At posting the service builds the AP journal entry (Dr expense/asset lines +
47	    Dr input tax, Cr AP control gross), sets ``journal_entry_id`` + ``open_amount`` = gross, and
48	    flips ``status`` to POSTED. ``open_amount`` (transaction currency) is the still-owed balance,
49	    reduced by payment allocations until PAID. Audited (D-010): a financial document."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "fin_vendor_bills"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        tenant_unique(),
54	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
55	        document_fk(),
56	        # The AP control account this bill credits (composite tenant FK). Bills carry their own
57	        # AP control account so the sub-ledger needs no fixed default (D-029).
58	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "ap_account_id"),
59	        # The journal entry created at posting (composite tenant FK; NULL until posted).
60	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),
61	        # Hot-list filter combination for GET /vendor-bills, aging, and payment runs
62	        # (PERFORMANCE §1, #25): tenant leads, then the dominant filters, then the sort key.
63	        sa.Index(
64	            "ix_fin_vendor_bills_list_filters",
65	            "tenant_id",
66	            "partner_id",
67	            "status",
68	            "bill_date",
69	        ),
70	    )

72	    partner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
73	    partner_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
74	    # The vendor's own reference on the bill (free text, not the system number); nullable.
75	    bill_external_ref: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
76	    # The gapless system number, claimed at posting (NULL until then; D-012).
77	    bill_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)

83	    )

85	    journal_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
86	    gross_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
87	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
88	    )

91	    )

94	    )

96	    # payment allocations until 0 (PAID). No stored total elsewhere — aging projects over this.
97	    open_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(

99	    )

105	    debits at posting; ``tax_code_id`` (nullable) drives the input-tax calculation, with the
106	    resulting ``tax_amount`` posted to the tax code's receivable account. ``cost_center_id`` and

117	            name="uq_fin_vendor_bill_lines_tenant_id_bill_id_line_number",

123	        tenant_fk("fin_tax_codes", "tax_code_id"),
124	    )

127	    line_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
128	    account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
129	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
130	    net_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
131	    tax_code_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
132	    tax_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(

134	    )

136	    project_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)

141	    journal entry (Dr AP control for the sum cleared, Cr bank for ``amount``, plus a realized-FX
142	    gain/loss line when the bill rate differs from the payment rate, D-019), then claims the gapless
143	    ``payment_number`` (D-012) and links the payment to the bills it clears. ``partner_id`` is the
144	    OPAQUE vendor id (D-029); ``bank_account_id`` is the bank/cash account credited. Audited

153	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),
154	    )

156	    partner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
157	    partner_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
158	    payment_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
159	    payment_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
160	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
19	"""
20	
21	import uuid
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	
24	import sqlalchemy as sa
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column

29	from app.core.models import (
30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,
32	    TimestampMixin,
33	    UuidPKMixin,
34	    tenant_fk,
35	)

37	# Depth ceiling on chain traversal (D-012): real chains are <10 nodes; the cap plus the
38	# visited-path cycle guard make a malformed graph terminate instead of spinning.
39	_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 20

41	
42	class Document(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
43	    """Registry entry for one business document (D-012). ``doc_type`` is a namespaced
44	    constant (``'sales.order'``, ``'finance.journal_entry'``) declared in module
45	    constants.py; ``doc_id`` is the PK of the business row in its own table; ``doc_number``
46	    is assigned at posting (NULL until then); ``status`` is the registry-level status string.
47	
48	    Not AuditMixin: the registry mirrors business rows that are themselves audited — the
49	    document's own table carries the audited business state, so auditing the registry too
50	    would double-record (documented exclusion)."""
51	
52	    __tablename__ = "core_documents"
53	    __table_args__ = (
54	        # One registry row per business document. Explicit name (D-022 convention keys on
55	        # column 0 only and would collide with tenant_unique()).
56	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
57	            "tenant_id", "doc_type", "doc_id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_type_doc_id"
58	        ),
59	        # Required so business rows can reference a registry entry via the composite tenant FK
60	        # (D-007 item 4) — DocumentMixin.document_fk() targets this.
61	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id"),
62	        # Partial unique index: a tenant may have many UNNUMBERED documents (doc_number NULL)
63	        # but never two with the SAME doc_number. Both dialect kwargs are required — Postgres
64	        # and SQLite each need their own (D-012 / D-021 dialect-kwargs pattern); a plain
65	        # UNIQUE would (incorrectly) reject multiple NULLs on some engines.
66	        sa.Index(
67	            "uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_number",
68	            "tenant_id",
69	            "doc_number",
70	            unique=True,
71	            postgresql_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
72	            sqlite_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
73	        ),
74	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
75	    )
76	
77	    doc_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
78	    doc_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
79	    doc_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
80	    status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)

83	class DocumentLink(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
84	    """A predecessor -> successor edge between two registry entries (D-012). ``link_type``
85	    names the relationship (``'fulfills'``, ``'invoices'``, ``'reverses'``, ``'posts'``).
86	    Both endpoints carry the composite tenant FK backstop so an edge can never span tenants.
87	    A CHECK forbids self-edges (a document cannot be its own predecessor)."""
88	
89	    __tablename__ = "core_doc_links"
90	    __table_args__ = (
91	        # One edge per (tenant, predecessor, successor). Explicit name (D-022 column-0 rule).
92	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
93	            "tenant_id",
94	            "predecessor_document_id",
95	            "successor_document_id",
96	            name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id_predecessor_document_id_successor",
97	        ),
98	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id"),
99	        # Pass the bare token: the D-022 ck convention wraps it as
100	        # ck_<table>_<constraint_name> -> ck_core_doc_links_no_self_link (matches 0006).
101	        sa.CheckConstraint(
102	            "predecessor_document_id != successor_document_id",
103	            name="no_self_link",
104	        ),
105	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
106	        # Both endpoints reference core_documents through the composite tenant FK, so the
107	        # D-022 column-0 convention would name both identically (collision). Spell out
108	        # distinct names that match migration 0006 exactly.
109	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
110	            ["tenant_id", "predecessor_document_id"],
111	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
112	            name="fk_core_doc_links_tenant_id_core_documents",
113	        ),
114	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
115	            ["tenant_id", "successor_document_id"],
116	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
117	            name="fk_core_doc_links_successor_document_id_core_documents",
118	        ),
119	    )
120	
121	    predecessor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
122	    successor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
123	    link_type: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)
124	
125	
126	def document_fk() -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
127	    """Composite tenant-safe FK for a business table's ``document_id`` -> core_documents
128	    (D-007 item 4). A business model that mixes in DocumentMixin adds this to its
129	    __table_args__ so the link can never point at another tenant's registry row, mirroring
130	    the tenant_fk()/tenant_unique() pattern in core/models.py."""
131	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
132	        ["tenant_id", "document_id"],
133	        ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
134	    )
135	
136	
137	class DocumentMixin:
138	    """Business-document link mixin (D-012). A business model mixes this in to get a NOT NULL
139	    ``document_id`` column tying its row to its registry entry — so the row CANNOT be inserted
140	    without first registering the document (the dual-write discipline D-012 relies on). The
141	    consuming model must also add ``document_fk()`` to its __table_args__ for the composite
142	    tenant-safe FK (a mixin cannot inject a multi-column FK into the host's __table_args__,
143	    exactly as TenantMixin needs the model to add tenant_fk()). UNIQUE so the registry-to-row
144	    mapping is 1:1.
145	
146	    Usage in a later module model:
147	
148	        class SalesOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
149	            __tablename__ = "sls_orders"
150	            __table_args__ = (tenant_unique(), tenant_fk("adm_tenants"), document_fk())
151	    """
152	
153	    @declared_attr
154	    def document_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
155	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, unique=True)
156	
157	
158	@dataclass(frozen=True)
159	class ChainNode:
160	    """One document in a flow chain — the registry projection the DocFlowViewer renders."""
161	
162	    document_id: uuid.UUID
163	    doc_type: str
164	    doc_id: uuid.UUID
165	    doc_number: str | None
166	    status: str | None
167

170	class ChainEdge:
171	    """One predecessor -> successor edge in a flow chain."""
172	
173	    predecessor_document_id: uuid.UUID
174	    successor_document_id: uuid.UUID
175	    link_type: str | None
176	
177	
178	@dataclass(frozen=True)
179	class DocumentChain:
180	    """Full bidirectional flow chain around a document: every connected node plus every edge
181	    among them. Usable directly by the read API (nodes + edges for the viewer)."""
182	
183	    nodes: list[ChainNode]
184	    edges: list[ChainEdge]

186	
187	async def register_document(
188	    session: AsyncSession,
189	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
190	    doc_type: str,
191	    doc_id: uuid.UUID,
192	    *,
193	    doc_number: str | None = None,
194	    status: str | None = None,
195	) -> Document:
196	    """Insert a registry row for a business document and return it (D-012). Called by the
197	    creating service in the same transaction as the business-row insert (the DocumentMixin
198	    NOT NULL FK makes skipping it a hard error). ``doc_number`` is left NULL for draft-
199	    lifecycle documents (numbered later at posting) and set for documents permanent at
200	    creation. A Core insert sets tenant_id explicitly — core/docflow is a D-007 sanctioned
201	    raw-SQL site."""
202	    document_id = uuid.uuid4()
203	    await session.execute(
204	        sa.insert(Document.__table__).values(
205	            id=document_id,
206	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
207	            doc_type=doc_type,
208	            doc_id=doc_id,
209	            doc_number=doc_number,
210	            status=status,
211	        )
212	    )
213	    return (
214	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id == document_id))
215	    ).scalar_one()
216	
217	
218	async def set_document_status(
219	    session: AsyncSession,
220	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
221	    document_id: uuid.UUID,
222	    *,
223	    status: str | None = None,
224	    doc_number: str | None = None,
225	) -> None:
226	    """Update a registry row's status and/or doc_number in the owning transaction (D-012).
227	
228	    The number is assigned at the moment a draft-lifecycle document becomes permanent (journal
229	    posting) — passing ``doc_number`` here writes it through the partial-unique (tenant,
230	    doc_number) backstop, so any numbering bug surfaces as a constraint violation. Only the
231	    provided arguments are changed (``None`` leaves the column untouched, except doc_number which
232	    is always set when supplied). A Core UPDATE addressed by (tenant_id, id) — a D-007 sanctioned
233	    explicit-tenant raw-SQL site."""
234	    values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
235	    if status is not None:
236	        values["status"] = status
237	    if doc_number is not None:
238	        values["doc_number"] = doc_number
239	    if not values:
240	        return
241	    await session.execute(
242	        sa.update(Document.__table__)
243	        .where(
244	            Document.__table__.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
245	            Document.__table__.c.id == document_id,
246	        )
247	        .values(**values)
248	    )
249	
250	
251	async def link_documents(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    predecessor: uuid.UUID,
255	    successor: uuid.UUID,
256	    link_type: str | None = None,
257	) -> DocumentLink:
258	    """Create a predecessor -> successor edge and return it (D-012). The UNIQUE(tenant_id,
259	    predecessor, successor) constraint rejects a duplicate edge as an IntegrityError, and
260	    the composite tenant FKs reject endpoints from another tenant. A Core insert sets
261	    tenant_id explicitly (D-007 sanctioned site)."""
262	    link_id = uuid.uuid4()
263	    await session.execute(
264	        sa.insert(DocumentLink.__table__).values(
265	            id=link_id,
266	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
267	            predecessor_document_id=predecessor,
268	            successor_document_id=successor,
269	            link_type=link_type,
270	        )
271	    )
272	    return (
273	        await session.execute(select(DocumentLink).where(DocumentLink.id == link_id))
274	    ).scalar_one()
275	
276	
277	def _build_reachability_cte(
278	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID, start: uuid.UUID, *, forward: bool
279	) -> sa.sql.Selectable:
280	    """One recursive CTE collecting every document reachable from ``start`` in ONE direction.
281	
282	    ``forward=True`` walks successor edges (descendants), ``forward=False`` walks predecessor
283	    edges (ancestors). The recursive member carries a ``depth`` column capped at
284	    _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and a ``path`` string of visited ids; the join excludes any node already
285	    on the path, so a diamond or cycle is traversed once and terminates (D-012 visited-path
286	    guard). Works identically on Postgres and SQLite (both support WITH RECURSIVE).
287	    """
288	    links = DocumentLink.__table__
289	    near = links.c.successor_document_id if forward else links.c.predecessor_document_id
290	    far = links.c.predecessor_document_id if forward else links.c.successor_document_id
291	
292	    # Anchor: the start node itself at depth 0. The path representation MUST match how the
293	    # recursive step casts ids (CAST(<Uuid column> AS VARCHAR)), so the start id is cast the
294	    # same way — casting a Uuid-typed literal renders dashless hex on SQLite and dashed on
295	    # PG, exactly as the column cast does, keeping the visited-path guard's LIKE comparison
296	    # apples-to-apples on both engines (a raw str(start) would carry dashes on SQLite and
297	    # silently defeat the guard).
298	    anchor = select(
299	        sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid).label("document_id"),
300	        sa.literal(0).label("depth"),
301	        sa.cast(sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid), sa.String).label("path"),
302	    ).cte("reach", recursive=True)
303	
304	    # Recursive step: from each frontier node, follow edges in the chosen direction to the
305	    # node on the other end, within the tenant, skipping nodes already on the path.
306	    step = (
307	        select(
308	            far.label("document_id"),
309	            (anchor.c.depth + 1).label("depth"),
310	            (anchor.c.path + sa.literal(",") + sa.cast(far, sa.String)).label("path"),
311	        )
312	        .select_from(anchor.join(links, near == anchor.c.document_id))
313	        .where(
314	            links.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	            anchor.c.depth < _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH,
316	            anchor.c.path.notlike(sa.literal("%") + sa.cast(far, sa.String) + sa.literal("%")),
317	        )
318	    )
319	    return anchor.union_all(step)
320	
321	
322	async def get_document_chain(
323	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
324	) -> DocumentChain:
325	    """Traverse the full flow chain around ``document_id`` in BOTH directions and return its
326	    nodes + edges (D-012). Two recursive CTEs (ancestors via predecessor edges, descendants
327	    via successor edges) collect every reachable registry id; their union is the connected
328	    component containing the start node. Edges are the links whose BOTH endpoints fall in that
329	    set. Cycles and diamonds are handled by the per-CTE visited-path guard, so each node and
330	    edge appears once. Returns empty nodes/edges when the id is unknown to this tenant.
331	
332	    Tenant isolation: the CTEs filter links by tenant_id and the registry/edge reads run
333	    under the caller's tenant context (the D-007 ORM filter), so a chain query never returns
334	    another tenant's documents.
335	    """
336	    ancestors = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=False)
337	    descendants = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=True)
338	
339	    ancestor_ids = set(
340	        (await session.execute(select(ancestors.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
341	    )
342	    descendant_ids = set(
343	        (await session.execute(select(descendants.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
344	    )
345	    reachable = ancestor_ids | descendant_ids
346	
347	    # An unknown id reaches only itself; if it is not a real registry row for this tenant,
348	    # there are no nodes to return — surface an empty chain (the router maps that to 404).
349	    document_rows = (
350	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id.in_(reachable)))
351	    ).scalars().all()
352	    if not document_rows:
353	        return DocumentChain(nodes=[], edges=[])
354	
355	    present_ids = {row.id for row in document_rows}
356	    nodes = [
357	        ChainNode(
358	            document_id=row.id,
359	            doc_type=row.doc_type,
360	            doc_id=row.doc_id,
361	            doc_number=row.doc_number,
362	            status=row.status,
363	        )
364	        for row in document_rows
365	    ]
366	
367	    link_rows = (
368	        await session.execute(
369	            select(DocumentLink).where(
370	                DocumentLink.predecessor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
371	                DocumentLink.successor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
372	            )
373	        )
374	    ).scalars().all()
375	    edges = [
376	        ChainEdge(
377	            predecessor_document_id=link.predecessor_document_id,
378	            successor_document_id=link.successor_document_id,
379	            link_type=link.link_type,
380	        )
381	        for link in link_rows
382	    ]
383	
384	    return DocumentChain(nodes=nodes, edges=edges)
385

1	"""D-012 gapless per-tenant document numbering.
2	
3	One half of the merged registry+numbering subsystem (the other half is core/docflow.py).
4	A document number is claimed INSIDE the business transaction that makes the document
5	permanent (drafts are numbered at posting). Because the counter increment and the
6	document insert commit or roll back together, gaplessness for committed documents falls
7	out of ACID with no burned-number reconciliation state (D-012 claim-timing rule).
8	
9	The atomic claim is a single ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
10	... RETURNING next_value`` — one portable statement that takes the row lock and reads the
11	new counter in one round trip. RETURNING is verified working on the project's aiosqlite
12	(SQLite >= 3.35; this build runs 3.53) and on Postgres, so no SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback
13	is needed (D-012 sanctioned the fallback only if RETURNING were unavailable).
14	
15	The ORM model lives HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is at ~273 lines and
16	adding the numbering + docflow entities would push it over the ~350-line soft cap, so the
17	D-012 entities sit in their concern files (numbering.py / docflow.py) — a placement the
18	PLAN sanctions explicitly and STRUCTURE §2 permits ("one concept per file": the sequence
19	concept lives with its claim logic). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
20	"""
21	
22	import uuid
23	from datetime import date
24	
25	import sqlalchemy as sa
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
29	
30	from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError
31	from app.core.models import (
32	    Base,
33	    TenantMixin,
34	    TimestampMixin,
35	    UuidPKMixin,
36	    tenant_fk,
37	)
38	
39	
40	class NumberSequence(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
41	    """Per-tenant gapless counter for one document kind (D-012).
42	
43	    ``name`` is the namespaced sequence key (e.g. ``'finance.invoice'``); a claim formats
44	    ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded next_value}`` (e.g. ``INV-2026-00001``). When ``year_reset``
45	    is set the running number restarts at 1 each calendar year and the year segment is
46	    rendered; ``current_year`` records which year the counter currently belongs to so the
47	    first claim of a new year resets it on demand (no rollover job, per D-012). Not
48	    AuditMixin: sequence rows are infrastructure counters mutated on every claim, not
49	    business state — auditing every increment would be noise (documented exclusion)."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "core_number_sequences"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        # One sequence per (tenant, name). Explicit name: the D-022 convention keys on
54	        # column 0 (tenant_id) only and would collide with tenant_unique() below.
55	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "name", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id_name"),
56	        # UNIQUE(tenant_id, id) so other tenant-scoped tables could reference a sequence via
57	        # the composite-FK backstop if ever needed (D-007 item 4).
58	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id"),
59	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
60	    )
61	
62	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
63	    prefix: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=False)
64	    padding: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
65	    # Next number to hand out. The atomic claim does next_value = next_value + 1 RETURNING
66	    # the post-increment value, so the FIRST claim of a sequence at next_value=1 returns 1.
67	    next_value: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=1, server_default=sa.text("1")
69	    )
70	    year_reset: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
71	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
72	    )
73	    # The year the running counter belongs to (NULL when year_reset is off).
74	    current_year: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=True)
75	
76	
77	def _format_number(prefix: str, padding: int, value: int, year: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Render ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded value}`` — the year segment is present only when
79	    the sequence year-resets (D-012). e.g. ('INV', 5, 1, 2026) -> 'INV-2026-00001'."""
80	    padded = str(value).zfill(padding)
81	    if year is None:
82	        return f"{prefix}-{padded}"
83	    return f"{prefix}-{year}-{padded}"
84	
85	
86	async def ensure_sequence(
87	    session: AsyncSession,
88	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    name: str,
90	    prefix: str,
91	    padding: int,
92	    year_reset: bool,
93	) -> NumberSequence:
94	    """Idempotent creator for provisioning/seed (D-012: year rollover and sequence setup
95	    need no job — the row is created on demand). Returns the existing row unchanged if the
96	    (tenant, name) sequence already exists, otherwise inserts it at next_value=1.
97	
98	    A Core insert is used (not an ORM add) so the tenant_id is set explicitly and the row
99	    is not subject to ORM tenant stamping — consistent with the D-007 sanction that core/
100	    numbering writes carry tenant_id explicitly. Callers run under the target tenant context
101	    or system_context (provisioning)."""
102	    existing = (
103	        await session.execute(
104	            select(NumberSequence).where(
105	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
106	            )
107	        )
108	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
109	    if existing is not None:
110	        return existing
111	
112	    current_year = date.today().year if year_reset else None
113	    await session.execute(
114	        sa.insert(NumberSequence.__table__).values(
115	            id=uuid.uuid4(),
116	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
117	            name=name,
118	            prefix=prefix,
119	            padding=padding,
120	            next_value=1,
121	            year_reset=year_reset,
122	            current_year=current_year,
123	        )
124	    )
125	    return (
126	        await session.execute(
127	            select(NumberSequence).where(
128	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
129	            )
130	        )
131	    ).scalar_one()
132	
133	
134	async def claim_number(
135	    session: AsyncSession,
136	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    sequence_name: str,
138	    *,
139	    on_date: date,
140	) -> str:
141	    """Atomically claim the next number for ``sequence_name`` and return the formatted
142	    string (D-012). The claim runs in the CALLER's transaction — the number is permanent
143	    only when that transaction commits, so a rollback returns the value to the pool and the
144	    next committed claim reuses it (gaplessness for committed documents).
145	
146	    Mechanism — one portable atomic statement per claim:
147	    ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
148	      WHERE tenant_id=:t AND name=:n RETURNING next_value`` — the RETURNING value is the
149	    post-increment counter; the row lock the UPDATE takes serializes concurrent claimers so
150	    two claims can never read the same number (verified on aiosqlite >= 3.35 and Postgres).
151	
152	    Year reset (when ``year_reset``): if ``on_date.year`` differs from the stored
153	    ``current_year``, the counter is reset to 1 for the new year FIRST (a guarded UPDATE
154	    that only fires while current_year is still the old value, so a concurrent claimer that
155	    reset it already cannot double-reset), then the normal atomic increment claims 1.
156	
157	    A Core UPDATE is used (bypasses the ORM tenant filter by design — core/ numbering is a
158	    D-007 sanctioned raw-SQL site with explicit tenant_id)."""
159	    sequence = (
160	        await session.execute(
161	            select(NumberSequence).where(
162	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == sequence_name
163	            )
164	        )
165	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
166	    if sequence is None:
167	        raise NotFoundError(
168	            message=f"Number sequence '{sequence_name}' is not configured for this tenant",
169	            code="core.number_sequence_missing",
170	        )
171	
172	    table = NumberSequence.__table__
173	    claim_year: int | None = None
174	    if sequence.year_reset:
175	        claim_year = on_date.year
176	        if sequence.current_year != claim_year:
177	            # Reset to 1 for the new year, guarded on the OLD current_year so a racing
178	            # claimer that already rolled the year over does not reset a second time.
179	            await session.execute(
180	                sa.update(table)
181	                .where(
182	                    table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
183	                    table.c.name == sequence_name,
184	                    table.c.current_year.is_not_distinct_from(sequence.current_year),
185	                )
186	                .values(next_value=1, current_year=claim_year)
187	            )
188	
189	    result = await session.execute(
190	        sa.update(table)
191	        .where(table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id, table.c.name == sequence_name)
192	        .values(next_value=table.c.next_value + 1)
193	        .returning(table.c.next_value)
194	    )
195	    next_after = result.scalar_one()
196	    claimed_value = next_after - 1
197	
198	    # The Core UPDATE changed the row out from under the loaded ORM object; expire it so its
199	    # attributes reload from the DB on next access rather than being marked dirty (which
200	    # would trigger a redundant ORM UPDATE on the next flush).
201	    formatted = _format_number(sequence.prefix, sequence.padding, claimed_value, claim_year)
202	    session.expire(sequence)
203	    return formatted

1	"""The stock-move WRITE engine (PLAN 5.2, D-020/D-036): create_move (the heart) + reverse_move.
2	
3	The read paths (``get_move``, ``list_moves``, ``list_on_hand``) live in ``stock_reads.py`` (split at
4	the 400-line cap); this module imports ``get_move`` from there and the package ``__init__``
5	re-exports both halves as one surface.
6	
7	A stock move is the quantity SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH and is POSTED-at-creation + IMMUTABLE — there
8	is no draft phase, no edit, no delete; a correction is a NEW reversing move (the universal-journal
9	reversal philosophy of D-017 applied to stock). ``create_move``:
10	
11	1. validates — item is STOCKED; the move_type's required bin sides are present (constants
12	   MOVE_BIN_SIDES; ADJUSTMENT = exactly one side; TRANSFER = two DIFFERENT bins); bins exist and
13	   belong to ACTIVE warehouses; quantity > 0; the item's tracking mode is satisfied (lot/serial
14	   resolved, created on a receipt, required-existing on issue/transfer; serial ⇒ quantity == 1);
15	2. registers the document + claims the gapless STK number (D-012, at creation — a move is permanent
16	   at create);
17	3. inserts the StockMove (POSTED);
18	4. updates the quant rows in the SAME transaction — decrement from_bin, increment to_bin — through
19	   ``apply_bin_delta`` (the CHECK >= 0 + the pre-flight check forbid negative stock, D-020);
20	   transfer deltas are applied in deterministic bin-id order (deadlock avoidance, D-020).
21	
22	The whole thing is one unit of work: move + quant updates commit or roll back together, so the
23	ledger and the projection can never disagree. Idempotency (D-013) is owned by the endpoint.
24	Inventory imports only finance/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5); this engine imports neither.
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import uuid
30	from datetime import date
31	from decimal import Decimal
32	
33	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
34	
35	from app.core import docflow
36	from app.core.events import publish
37	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
38	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
39	from app.modules.inventory.constants import (
40	    MOVE_BIN_SIDES,
41	    STOCK_MOVE_DOC_TYPE,
42	    STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PADDING,
43	    STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PREFIX,
44	    STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK,
45	    STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME,
46	    ItemType,
47	    MoveStatus,
48	    MoveType,
49	    TrackingMode,
50	)
51	from app.modules.inventory.models import Bin, Item, StockMove
52	from app.modules.inventory.schemas import StockMoveCreate
53	from app.modules.inventory.service import costing, costing_reversal
54	from app.modules.inventory.service.stock_quants import (
55	    apply_bin_delta,
56	    resolve_lot,
57	    resolve_serial,
58	)
59	from app.modules.inventory.service.stock_reads import get_move
