62	async def _require_stocked_item(
63	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
64	) -> Item:
65	    item = await session.get(Item, item_id)
66	    if item is None or item.tenant_id != tenant_id:
67	        raise NotFoundError(message="Item not found", code="inventory.item_not_found")
68	    if ItemType(item.item_type) != ItemType.STOCKED:
69	        raise ValidationFailedError(
70	            message="Only stocked items participate in stock moves",
71	            code="inventory.item_not_stocked",
72	            details={"item_id": str(item_id), "item_type": item.item_type},
73	        )
74	    return item
75	
76	
77	async def _require_active_bin(
78	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bin_id: uuid.UUID, *, side: str
79	) -> Bin:
80	    """The bin exists, belongs to this tenant, and its warehouse is active. A move never lands stock
81	    in (or pulls from) a bin whose warehouse was deactivated."""
82	    bin_row = await session.get(Bin, bin_id)
83	    if bin_row is None or bin_row.tenant_id != tenant_id:
84	        raise ValidationFailedError(
85	            message=f"The {side} bin does not exist",
86	            code="inventory.bin_not_found",
87	            details={"bin_id": str(bin_id), "side": side},
88	        )
89	    if not bin_row.is_active:
90	        raise ValidationFailedError(
91	            message=f"The {side} bin is inactive",
92	            code="inventory.bin_inactive",
93	            details={"bin_id": str(bin_id), "side": side},
94	        )
95	    return bin_row
96	
97	
98	def _validate_bin_sides(
99	    move_type: MoveType, from_bin_id: uuid.UUID | None, to_bin_id: uuid.UUID | None
100	) -> None:
101	    """Enforce the move_type ⇒ required-bin-side rule (constants.MOVE_BIN_SIDES). ADJUSTMENT is the
102	    special case: EXACTLY ONE side. TRANSFER additionally requires the two bins to differ."""
103	    if move_type == MoveType.ADJUSTMENT:
104	        if (from_bin_id is None) == (to_bin_id is None):
105	            raise ValidationFailedError(
106	                message="An adjustment sets exactly one of from_bin / to_bin",
107	                code="inventory.adjustment_one_side",
108	            )
109	        return
110	    from_required, to_required = MOVE_BIN_SIDES[move_type]
111	    if from_required and from_bin_id is None:
112	        raise ValidationFailedError(
113	            message=f"{move_type.value} requires a from_bin",
114	            code="inventory.move_from_bin_required",
115	        )
116	    if not from_required and from_bin_id is not None:
117	        raise ValidationFailedError(
118	            message=f"{move_type.value} must not set a from_bin",
119	            code="inventory.move_from_bin_forbidden",
120	        )
121	    if to_required and to_bin_id is None:
122	        raise ValidationFailedError(
123	            message=f"{move_type.value} requires a to_bin",
124	            code="inventory.move_to_bin_required",
125	        )
126	    if not to_required and to_bin_id is not None:
127	        raise ValidationFailedError(
128	            message=f"{move_type.value} must not set a to_bin",
129	            code="inventory.move_to_bin_forbidden",
130	        )
131	    if move_type == MoveType.TRANSFER and from_bin_id == to_bin_id:
132	        raise ValidationFailedError(
133	            message="A transfer must move between two different bins",
134	            code="inventory.transfer_same_bin",
135	        )
136	
137	
138	def _is_inbound(move_type: MoveType, to_bin_id: uuid.UUID | None) -> bool:
139	    """Whether the move adds stock (the costing-inbound side): a RECEIPT, or a positive ADJUSTMENT
140	    (to_bin set). The inbound side is where the REQUIRED entry unit_cost applies (D-020)."""
141	    return move_type == MoveType.RECEIPT or (
142	        move_type == MoveType.ADJUSTMENT and to_bin_id is not None
143	    )
144	
145	
146	def _validate_unit_cost(payload: StockMoveCreate, move_type: MoveType) -> Decimal | None:
147	    """Costing input rule (D-020): a RECEIPT / positive ADJUSTMENT REQUIRES ``unit_cost`` (the value
148	    stock enters at, > 0). An ISSUE / negative ADJUSTMENT / TRANSFER IGNORE any passed cost — the
149	    engine computes the outbound cost / carries the current valuation — so the move stores it as
150	    None
151	    and the engine fills it. Returns the validated entry cost (None for the computed sides)."""
152	    if _is_inbound(move_type, payload.to_bin_id):
153	        if payload.unit_cost is None or Decimal(payload.unit_cost) <= 0:
154	            raise ValidationFailedError(
155	                message="A receipt or stock-increase requires a positive unit cost",
156	                code="inventory.receipt_unit_cost_required",
157	            )
158	        return Decimal(payload.unit_cost)
159	    return None
160	
161	
162	async def _apply_quant_deltas(
163	    session: AsyncSession,
164	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
165	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
166	    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None,
167	    from_bin_id: uuid.UUID | None,
168	    to_bin_id: uuid.UUID | None,
169	    quantity: Decimal,
170	) -> None:
171	    """Update the maintained quant projection for one move (D-036): decrement from_bin, increment
172	    to_bin. The two sides are applied in deterministic bin-id order (deadlock avoidance, D-020:
173	    concurrent movers touching the same pair lock it in the same order). A decrement raises
174	    InsufficientStockError if it would go negative (no-negative-stock, D-020)."""
175	    deltas: list[tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]] = []
176	    if from_bin_id is not None:
177	        deltas.append((from_bin_id, -quantity))
178	    if to_bin_id is not None:
179	        deltas.append((to_bin_id, quantity))
180	    # Lock/update in ascending bin-id order so two concurrent transfers between the same bins
181	    # never deadlock by locking the pair in opposite orders (D-020 deadlock avoidance).
182	    for bin_id, delta in sorted(deltas, key=lambda pair: pair[0].bytes):
183	        await apply_bin_delta(session, tenant_id, item_id, bin_id, lot_id, delta)
184	
185	
186	async def create_move(
187	    session: AsyncSession,
188	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
189	    payload: StockMoveCreate,
190	    *,
191	    reversal_of: StockMove | None = None,
192	) -> StockMove:
193	    """Create + POST a stock move (the heart, PLAN 5.2/5.3). Validates everything (see module
194	    docstring), claims the gapless STK number, inserts the POSTED move, updates the quant
195	    projection,
196	    runs COSTING and publishes the valuation event — all in the SAME transaction (D-020). Raises 422
197	    InsufficientStockError when an issue/transfer exceeds on-hand; NotFound for a missing item; 422
198	    for a non-stocked item or a bin-side rule break. The caller commits via uow.
199	
200	    ``reversal_of`` (set by ``reverse_move``) runs the costing REVERSAL path instead of a fresh
201	    valuation: the reversing move replays the original's FIFO consumptions / re-applies its
202	    moving-average value and emits the OPPOSITE valuation event so the COGS journal is reversed too
203	    (D-020)."""
204	    move_type = MoveType(payload.move_type)
205	    quantity = Decimal(payload.quantity)
206	    if quantity <= 0:
207	        raise ValidationFailedError(
208	            message="Move quantity must be greater than zero",
209	            code="inventory.move_quantity_invalid",
210	            details={"quantity": str(quantity)},
211	        )
212	
213	    item = await _require_stocked_item(session, tenant_id, payload.item_id)
214	    _validate_bin_sides(move_type, payload.from_bin_id, payload.to_bin_id)
215	    # Costing input (D-020): a RECEIPT/positive-ADJUSTMENT requires the entry cost; computed sides
216	    # ignore it. Validated BEFORE any write so a missing cost fails fast (no number burned). A
217	    # reversal carries its cost from the original move (the costing reversal path), so it does not
218	    # need (and does not pass) an entry cost — skip the requirement.
219	    entry_cost = None if reversal_of is not None else _validate_unit_cost(payload, move_type)
220	    if payload.from_bin_id is not None:
221	        await _require_active_bin(session, tenant_id, payload.from_bin_id, side="from")
222	    if payload.to_bin_id is not None:
223	        await _require_active_bin(session, tenant_id, payload.to_bin_id, side="to")
224	
225	    # A receipt MAY create a lot/serial master instance (5.1 deferred that to receipts); an
226	    # issue/transfer/adjustment-decrease must reference one that already exists with stock.
227	    create_instance = move_type == MoveType.RECEIPT
228	    lot_id = await resolve_lot(
229	        session,
230	        tenant_id,
231	        item,
232	        lot_id=payload.lot_id,
233	        lot_code=payload.lot_code,
234	        create_if_missing=create_instance,
235	    )
236	    serial_id = await resolve_serial(
237	        session,
238	        tenant_id,
239	        item,
240	        serial_id=payload.serial_id,
241	        serial_code=payload.serial_code,
242	        create_if_missing=create_instance,
243	    )
244	    if TrackingMode(item.tracking_mode) == TrackingMode.SERIAL and quantity != 1:
245	        raise ValidationFailedError(
246	            message="A serial-tracked move has quantity 1 (a serial moves wholesale)",
247	            code="inventory.serial_quantity_invalid",
248	            details={"quantity": str(quantity)},
249	        )
250	
251	    move_date = payload.move_date or date.today()
252	    move_id = uuid.uuid4()
253	    document = await docflow.register_document(
254	        session,
255	        tenant_id,
256	        STOCK_MOVE_DOC_TYPE,
257	        move_id,
258	        doc_number=None,
259	        status=MoveStatus.POSTED.value,
260	    )
261	    # A move is permanent at creation (POSTED immediately), so the number is claimed now (D-012
262	    # claim-at-permanence, the orders/receipts branch, not the draft branch).
263	    await ensure_sequence(
264	        session,
265	        tenant_id,
266	        STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME,
267	        STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PREFIX,
268	        STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PADDING,
269	        year_reset=True,
270	    )
271	    move_number = await claim_number(
272	        session, tenant_id, STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=move_date
273	    )
274	
275	    move = StockMove(
276	        id=move_id,
277	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
278	        document_id=document.id,
279	        move_number=move_number,
280	        move_type=move_type.value,
281	        item_id=item.id,
282	        quantity=quantity,
283	        base_uom_id=item.base_uom_id,
284	        from_bin_id=payload.from_bin_id,
285	        to_bin_id=payload.to_bin_id,
286	        lot_id=lot_id,
287	        serial_id=serial_id,
288	        move_date=move_date,
289	        reference=payload.reference,
290	        posted=True,
291	        # The validated entry cost on an inbound move; the costing engine fills the computed cost on
292	        # an outbound/transfer move below (D-020).
293	        unit_cost=entry_cost,
294	    )
295	    session.add(move)
296	    await session.flush()
297	
298	    await docflow.set_document_status(
299	        session, tenant_id, document.id, doc_number=move_number, status=MoveStatus.POSTED.value
300	    )
301	    await _apply_quant_deltas(
302	        session,
303	        tenant_id,
304	        item.id,
305	        lot_id,
306	        payload.from_bin_id,
307	        payload.to_bin_id,
308	        quantity,
309	    )
310	    # Costing IN THE SAME TRANSACTION (D-020), right after the quant update: update the
311	    # moving-average valuation / FIFO layers, write the computed cost onto the move, and publish the
312	    # StockValued event BEFORE the uow drains it — the COGS/inventory journal posts in this same
313	    # transaction, so the move + quant + valuation + journal commit or roll back as one. A
314	    # value-neutral within-warehouse transfer returns no event (no journal).
315	    if reversal_of is not None:
316	        result = await costing_reversal.reverse_costing(
317	            session, tenant_id, item, move, reversal_of
318	        )
319	    else:
320	        result = await costing.apply_costing(session, tenant_id, item, move)
321	    if result.event is not None:
322	        publish(session, result.event)
323	    return move
324	
325	
326	async def reverse_move(
327	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, move_id: uuid.UUID
328	) -> StockMove:
329	    """Reverse a posted move by posting an OPPOSITE move (PLAN 5.2): same item/quantity/lot/serial
330	    with from_bin and to_bin SWAPPED, linked to the original via docflow ('reverses'). The ledger
331	    stays append-only — corrections are new moves, never edits (D-017 philosophy). The reversing
332	    move restores the quants the original changed; a reversal that would itself go negative (the
333	    stock already left) raises InsufficientStockError like any other move. A move may be reversed
334	    once (a second reverse of the same original is rejected)."""
335	    original = await get_move(session, tenant_id, move_id)
336	    # Guard against double-reversal: a reversing move points back via docflow 'reverses'. Cheap
337	    # check — has any move already reversed this one?
338	    if await _already_reversed(session, tenant_id, original.document_id):
339	        raise ConflictError(
340	            message="This stock move has already been reversed",
341	            code="inventory.move_already_reversed",
342	        )
343	
344	    reversal_payload = StockMoveCreate(
345	        move_type=MoveType(original.move_type),
346	        item_id=original.item_id,
347	        quantity=Decimal(original.quantity),
348	        # Swap the directions so the reversing move undoes the original's quant deltas.
349	        from_bin_id=original.to_bin_id,
350	        to_bin_id=original.from_bin_id,
351	        lot_id=original.lot_id,
352	        serial_id=original.serial_id,
353	        move_date=date.today(),
354	        reference=f"Reversal of {original.move_number}",
355	    )
356	    # A reversal of a RECEIPT swaps to an ISSUE-shaped move (from set, to NULL) and vice versa; for
357	    # ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER the swap stays the same move_type. The bin-side validator accepts the
358	    # swapped shape because the move_type's required side follows the populated bin.
359	    reversal_payload = _retype_for_reversal(reversal_payload, MoveType(original.move_type))
360	
361	    # Pass the original so create_move runs the costing REVERSAL (replay), not a fresh valuation,
362	    # and
363	    # publishes the OPPOSITE StockValued event so the COGS journal is reversed in the same
364	    # transaction (D-020).
365	    reversal = await create_move(
366	        session, tenant_id, reversal_payload, reversal_of=original
367	    )
368	    await docflow.link_documents(
369	        session,
370	        tenant_id,
371	        predecessor=original.document_id,
372	        successor=reversal.document_id,
373	        link_type=STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK,
374	    )
375	    return reversal
376	
377	
378	def _retype_for_reversal(payload: StockMoveCreate, original_type: MoveType) -> StockMoveCreate:
379	    """A RECEIPT reverses as an ISSUE and an ISSUE as a RECEIPT (the bin sides flip, so the type
380	    must too, or the bin-side validator rejects the swapped shape). TRANSFER and ADJUSTMENT keep
381	    their type — a swapped TRANSFER is still a TRANSFER, and a swapped ADJUSTMENT (the single side
382	    moves to the other side) is still an ADJUSTMENT."""
383	    if original_type == MoveType.RECEIPT:
384	        return payload.model_copy(update={"move_type": MoveType.ISSUE})
385	    if original_type == MoveType.ISSUE:
386	        return payload.model_copy(update={"move_type": MoveType.RECEIPT})
387	    return payload
388	
389	
390	async def _already_reversed(
391	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
392	) -> bool:
393	    """Whether a 'reverses' edge already points FROM this move's document (it has been reversed)."""
394	    chain = await docflow.get_document_chain(session, tenant_id, document_id)
395	    return any(
396	        edge.link_type == STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK
397	        and edge.predecessor_document_id == document_id
398	        for edge in chain.edges
399	    )

1	"""Vendor-bill lifecycle: draft creation + posting through the journal (PLAN 4.5, AP).
2	
3	A vendor bill is the AP-side document. ``create_vendor_bill`` computes input tax (via the shared
4	tax engine) and totals on a DRAFT; ``post_vendor_bill`` builds and posts the AP journal entry
5	(Dr each expense/asset line net, Dr input tax to the tax code's receivable account, Cr the AP
6	control for the gross — with the opaque ``partner_id`` stamped on the AP line, D-029), claims the
7	gapless system number (D-012), links the bill document to its journal entry (docflow), sets
8	``open_amount`` = gross, and publishes ``VendorBillPosted``. Idempotent at the service level: a
9	re-post of an already-POSTED bill returns it unchanged.
10	
11	The journal engine handles FX translation at posting (D-019): a foreign-currency bill's functional
12	amounts are frozen at the posting-date SPOT rate by the same machinery every entry uses. Finance
13	stays the bottom dependency — this module imports no other module.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	from datetime import date
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	
22	from sqlalchemy import select
23	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
24	
25	from app.core import docflow
26	from app.core.events import publish
27	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
28	from app.core.money import quantize_for_currency
29	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
30	from app.modules.finance.constants import (
31	    AP_BILL_DOC_TYPE,
32	    AP_BILL_NUMBER_PADDING,
33	    AP_BILL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
34	    AP_BILL_POSTS_LINK,
35	    AP_BILL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
36	    AP_PARTNER_TYPE,
37	    BillStatus,
38	    DocumentType,
39	    TaxDirection,
40	)
41	from app.modules.finance.events import VendorBillPosted
42	from app.modules.finance.models import (
43	    Account,
44	    TaxCode,
45	    VendorBill,
46	    VendorBillLine,
47	)
48	from app.modules.finance.payables_schemas import VendorBillCreate
49	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate, JournalLineCreate
50	from app.modules.finance.service.journal import create_draft_entry, post_entry
51	from app.modules.finance.service.tax import calculate_line_tax
52	
53	
54	async def _require_account(
55	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, account_id: uuid.UUID, *, label: str
56	) -> Account:
57	    account = (
58	        await session.execute(
59	            select(Account).where(Account.tenant_id == tenant_id, Account.id == account_id)
60	        )
61	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
62	    if account is None:
63	        raise ValidationFailedError(
64	            message=f"The {label} account does not exist in this tenant",
65	            code="finance.ap_account_not_found",
66	            details={"account_id": str(account_id)},
67	        )
68	    return account
69	
70	
71	async def _tax_code(
72	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, tax_code_id: uuid.UUID
73	) -> TaxCode:
74	    tax_code = (
75	        await session.execute(
76	            select(TaxCode).where(TaxCode.tenant_id == tenant_id, TaxCode.id == tax_code_id)
77	        )
78	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
79	    if tax_code is None:
80	        raise ValidationFailedError(
81	            message="A line references an unknown tax code",
82	            code="finance.ap_tax_code_not_found",
83	            details={"tax_code_id": str(tax_code_id)},
84	        )
85	    return tax_code
86	
87	
88	async def get_vendor_bill(
89	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bill_id: uuid.UUID
90	) -> VendorBill:
91	    bill = await session.get(VendorBill, bill_id)
92	    if bill is None or bill.tenant_id != tenant_id:
93	        raise NotFoundError(message="Vendor bill not found", code="finance.vendor_bill_not_found")
94	    return bill
95	
96	
97	async def get_vendor_bill_lines(
98	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bill_id: uuid.UUID
99	) -> list[VendorBillLine]:
100	    stmt = (
101	        select(VendorBillLine)
102	        .where(VendorBillLine.tenant_id == tenant_id, VendorBillLine.bill_id == bill_id)
103	        .order_by(VendorBillLine.line_number)
104	    )
105	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
106	
107	
108	async def create_vendor_bill(
109	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: VendorBillCreate
110	) -> VendorBill:
111	    """Create a DRAFT vendor bill + lines (PLAN 4.5). Validates the AP control + every line account
112	    exists; computes input tax per line via the shared tax engine (so net/tax/gross match Sales/AR)
113	    and rolls up the bill totals. Registers the document in core_documents with NO number (claimed
114	    at posting, D-012). ``open_amount`` stays 0 until posting. Does NOT post a journal entry."""
115	    if not payload.lines:
116	        raise ValidationFailedError(
117	            message="A vendor bill needs at least one line",
118	            code="finance.vendor_bill_no_lines",
119	        )
120	    await _require_account(session, tenant_id, payload.ap_account_id, label="AP control")
121	
122	    gross_total = Decimal(0)
123	    tax_total = Decimal(0)
124	    net_total = Decimal(0)
125	    line_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
126	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
127	        await _require_account(session, tenant_id, line.account_id, label="line")
128	        net = quantize_for_currency(line.net_amount, payload.currency_code)
129	        tax_amount = Decimal(0)
130	        if line.tax_code_id is not None:
131	            tax_code = await _tax_code(session, tenant_id, line.tax_code_id)
132	            calc = calculate_line_tax(
133	                net, tax_code, direction=TaxDirection.INPUT, currency_code=payload.currency_code
134	            )
135	            net = calc.net_amount
136	            tax_amount = calc.tax_amount
137	        net_total += net
138	        tax_total += tax_amount
139	        gross_total += net + tax_amount
140	        line_rows.append(
141	            {
142	                "line_number": index,
143	                "account_id": line.account_id,
144	                "description": line.description,
145	                "net_amount": net,
146	                "tax_code_id": line.tax_code_id,
147	                "tax_amount": tax_amount,
148	                "cost_center_id": line.cost_center_id,
149	                "project_id": line.project_id,
150	            }
151	        )
152	
153	    bill_id = uuid.uuid4()
154	    document = await docflow.register_document(
155	        session,
156	        tenant_id,
157	        AP_BILL_DOC_TYPE,
158	        bill_id,
159	        doc_number=None,
160	        status=BillStatus.DRAFT.value,
161	    )
162	    bill = VendorBill(
163	        id=bill_id,
164	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
165	        document_id=document.id,
166	        partner_id=payload.partner_id,
167	        partner_name=payload.partner_name,
168	        bill_external_ref=payload.bill_external_ref,
169	        bill_date=payload.bill_date,
170	        due_date=payload.due_date,
171	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
172	        status=BillStatus.DRAFT.value,
173	        ap_account_id=payload.ap_account_id,
174	        gross_amount=gross_total,
175	        tax_amount=tax_total,
176	        net_amount=net_total,
177	        open_amount=Decimal(0),
178	        description=payload.description,
179	    )
180	    session.add(bill)
181	    for row in line_rows:
182	        session.add(VendorBillLine(tenant_id=tenant_id, bill_id=bill_id, **row))
183	    await session.flush()
184	    return bill
185	
186	
187	def _bill_journal_lines(
188	    bill: VendorBill, lines: list[VendorBillLine], tax_account_by_code: dict[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID]
189	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
190	    """The balanced AP journal lines for a bill (PLAN 4.5): Dr each line's net to its expense/asset
191	    account, Dr input tax to the tax code's receivable account (one line per line with tax), Cr the
192	    AP control for the gross — partner_id stamped on the AP line so the open item is partner-keyed
193	    (D-029). Dimensions ride to the journal line so CO projections see them."""
194	    journal_lines: list[JournalLineCreate] = []
195	    for line in lines:
196	        journal_lines.append(
197	            JournalLineCreate(
198	                account_id=line.account_id,
199	                description=line.description,
200	                transaction_debit_amount=line.net_amount,
201	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
202	                project_id=line.project_id,
203	            )
204	        )
205	        if line.tax_amount and line.tax_code_id is not None:
206	            journal_lines.append(
207	                JournalLineCreate(
208	                    account_id=tax_account_by_code[line.tax_code_id],
209	                    description="Input tax",
210	                    transaction_debit_amount=line.tax_amount,
211	                )
212	            )
213	    journal_lines.append(
214	        JournalLineCreate(
215	            account_id=bill.ap_account_id,
216	            description=f"AP {bill.partner_name}",
217	            transaction_credit_amount=bill.gross_amount,
218	            partner_type=AP_PARTNER_TYPE,
219	            partner_id=bill.partner_id,
220	        )
221	    )
222	    return journal_lines
223	
224	
225	async def _resolve_tax_accounts(
226	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, lines: list[VendorBillLine]
227	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID]:
228	    """Map each line's tax_code_id -> its receivable (INPUT) account (PLAN 4.5). Raises a clear 422
229	    if a code that levied tax has no receivable account wired (the tax engine would otherwise post
230	    to None)."""
231	    accounts: dict[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID] = {}
232	    for line in lines:
233	        if not line.tax_amount or line.tax_code_id is None or line.tax_code_id in accounts:
234	            continue
235	        tax_code = await _tax_code(session, tenant_id, line.tax_code_id)
236	        if tax_code.tax_receivable_account_id is None:
237	            raise ValidationFailedError(
238	                message=f"Tax code {tax_code.code} has no input-tax (receivable) account",
239	                code="finance.ap_tax_account_unwired",
240	                details={"tax_code_id": str(line.tax_code_id)},
241	            )
242	        accounts[line.tax_code_id] = tax_code.tax_receivable_account_id
243	    return accounts
244	
245	
246	async def post_vendor_bill(
247	    session: AsyncSession,
248	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
249	    bill_id: uuid.UUID,
250	    *,
251	    posting_date: date | None = None,
252	) -> VendorBill:
253	    """Post a DRAFT vendor bill to the journal (PLAN 4.5). Idempotent: an already-POSTED bill is
254	    returned unchanged. Builds the balanced AP entry (document_type AP_BILL), posts it via the
255	    journal engine (which claims the entry number, resolves the period, and translates FX at the
256	    posting rate, D-019), claims the bill's gapless system number, links bill->journal (docflow
257	    'posts'), sets ``open_amount`` = gross + status POSTED, and publishes ``VendorBillPosted``.
258	    ``posting_date`` defaults to the bill date."""
259	    bill = await get_vendor_bill(session, tenant_id, bill_id)
260	    if bill.status == BillStatus.POSTED.value:
261	        return bill
262	    if bill.status != BillStatus.DRAFT.value:
263	        raise ConflictError(
264	            message="Only a draft vendor bill can be posted",
265	            code="finance.vendor_bill_not_draft",
266	            details={"status": bill.status},
267	        )
268	
269	    lines = await get_vendor_bill_lines(session, tenant_id, bill_id)
270	    tax_account_by_code = await _resolve_tax_accounts(session, tenant_id, lines)
271	
272	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
273	        session,
274	        tenant_id,
275	        JournalEntryCreate(
276	            posting_date=posting_date or bill.bill_date,
277	            currency_code=bill.currency_code,
278	            description=f"Vendor bill {bill.partner_name}",
279	            document_type=DocumentType.AP_INVOICE,
280	            lines=_bill_journal_lines(bill, lines, tax_account_by_code),
281	        ),
282	    )
283	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, entry.id)
284	
285	    await ensure_sequence(
286	        session,
287	        tenant_id,
288	        AP_BILL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
289	        AP_BILL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
290	        AP_BILL_NUMBER_PADDING,
291	        year_reset=True,
292	    )
293	    bill_number = await claim_number(
294	        session, tenant_id, AP_BILL_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=bill.bill_date
295	    )
296	
297	    bill.bill_number = bill_number
298	    bill.journal_entry_id = entry.id
299	    bill.open_amount = bill.gross_amount
300	    bill.status = BillStatus.POSTED.value
301	    await session.flush()
302	
303	    await docflow.set_document_status(
304	        session, tenant_id, bill.document_id, status=BillStatus.POSTED.value, doc_number=bill_number
305	    )
306	    await docflow.link_documents(
307	        session,
308	        tenant_id,
309	        predecessor=bill.document_id,
310	        successor=entry.document_id,
311	        link_type=AP_BILL_POSTS_LINK,
312	    )
313	
314	    publish(
315	        session,
316	        VendorBillPosted(
317	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
318	            bill_id=bill.id,
319	            bill_number=bill_number,
320	            journal_entry_id=entry.id,
321	            partner_id=bill.partner_id,
322	            currency_code=bill.currency_code,
323	            gross_amount=bill.gross_amount,
324	            tax_amount=bill.tax_amount,
325	            net_amount=bill.net_amount,
326	        ),
327	    )
328	    return bill
329	
330	
331	async def list_vendor_bills(
332	    session: AsyncSession,
333	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
334	    *,
335	    cursor: str | None,
336	    limit: int,
337	    status: str | None = None,
338	    partner_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
339	) -> object:
340	    """Keyset-paginated bill list, newest bill_date first (D-014). ``status`` + ``partner_id``
341	    filters fold into the cursor fingerprint. Returns a ``Page`` of ORM objects."""
342	    from app.core.pagination import OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
343	
344	    stmt = select(VendorBill).where(VendorBill.tenant_id == tenant_id)
345	    if status is not None:
346	        stmt = stmt.where(VendorBill.status == BillStatus(status).value)
347	    if partner_id is not None:
348	        stmt = stmt.where(VendorBill.partner_id == partner_id)
349	    return await paginate(
350	        session,
351	        stmt,
352	        order_by=[
353	            OrderKey(VendorBill.bill_date, SortDirection.DESC),
354	            OrderKey(VendorBill.created_at, SortDirection.DESC),
355	        ],
356	        pk=VendorBill.id,
357	        cursor=cursor,
358	        limit=limit,
359	        filters=filter_fingerprint(status, partner_id),
360	    )

1	"""Finance models package (STRUCTURE §3: split into models/ once the combined file passed the
2	400-line cap). Re-exports every model so ``from app.modules.finance.models import Account`` and
3	``JournalEntry`` keep working from one surface, and so every importer (alembic env.py, the
4	tenancy mapper-enumeration suite) registers all tables on ``Base.metadata``.
5	
6	- ``accounts``: chart of accounts + fiscal years/periods (D-021, D-018).
7	- ``journal``: the universal journal header + lines (D-017).
8	- ``fx``: currencies, exchange rates, posting defaults, revaluation runs (D-019).

1	"""D-013 idempotency keys: reservation + atomic completion via route capture.
2	
3	The mechanism, exactly as D-013 prescribes, in two phases:
4	
5	* **Phase 1 (reserve).** ``Idempotent("endpoint")`` reads the ``Idempotency-Key`` header,
6	  hashes the canonical request body, and calls :func:`reserve`, which opens a SEPARATE
7	  short-lived session, INSERTs an ``IN_PROGRESS`` row, and COMMITs immediately. Two concurrent
8	  duplicates therefore collide on the natural composite PK ``(tenant_id, endpoint, key)`` — PG's
9	  unique index arbitrates, SQLite's single-writer lock serializes. On collision the existing row
10	  decides the outcome: ``COMPLETED`` + matching hash → REPLAY the stored response verbatim with
11	  header ``Idempotency-Replayed: true`` and no business logic; ``COMPLETED`` + different hash →
12	  422 ``idempotency.key_reuse`` (a client bug reusing a key for a different body); ``IN_PROGRESS``
13	  → 409 ``idempotency.in_progress`` (a concurrent duplicate is still running).
14	
15	* **Phase 2 (capture).** The dependency YIELDS an :class:`IdempotencyContext` bound to the
16	  request's BUSINESS session. The handler's last act is ``idem.capture(read_schema)`` — it
17	  ``model_dump``s the exact schema FastAPI will serialize and STAGES the completion UPDATE
18	  (status → COMPLETED, response_status, response_body, completed_at) on the business session, so
19	  the document and the replay record commit ATOMICALLY in one ``run_in_uow`` transaction. The
20	  cardinal invariant: a replayable response exists iff the document exists.
21	
22	* **Fail-closed.** On a BUSINESS EXCEPTION, the dependency's teardown deletes the dangling
23	  IN_PROGRESS reservation (committed in its own session) so the client may retry the same key, and
24	  re-raises — the app's exception handlers render the proper error envelope. (Atlas commits the
25	  business work via ``run_in_uow`` INSIDE the handler, so a failed handler has already rolled the
26	  document AND the staged capture UPDATE back; only the separately-committed reservation needs
27	  cleanup.) On a FORGOTTEN ``capture()`` (handler returned 2xx but never captured), the teardown
28	  deletes the dangling reservation and logs a server error; it cannot convert the already-sent 2xx
29	  to a 500 because the run_in_uow commit precedes teardown — a documented deviation from D-013's
30	  literal "teardown rolls back", which assumed a deferred session-dependency commit (DECISIONS.md).
31	
32	Replay short-circuit mechanism (FastAPI-idiomatic): :func:`reserve` raises
33	:class:`IdempotencyReplay` carrying the stored response. ``IdempotencyReplay`` is an
34	``AtlasError`` subtype whose dedicated handler in ``app.main`` writes the stored
35	status+body+header — so a completed-key replay never reaches the handler body and the side
36	effect cannot run twice. A first-time request instead yields the context normally.
37	"""

108	def compute_request_hash(body: bytes) -> str:
109	    """sha256 hex of the raw request body (D-013). The raw bytes are the canonical form here:
110	    a replay must present the byte-identical body, and hashing bytes avoids re-serialization
111	    ambiguity. An empty body hashes to the sha256 of b'' — stable and well-defined."""

115	class IdempotencyReplay(AtlasError):
116	    """Raised by reserve() when a COMPLETED key with a matching hash is replayed. NOT an error
117	    in the user sense — its dedicated handler in app.main writes the stored response verbatim
118	    (status + body + Idempotency-Replayed header), short-circuiting the route so the side effect
119	    never runs twice. status_code/details carry the stored response across to the handler."""
120	
121	    def __init__(self, response_status: int, response_body: Any) -> None:
122	        super().__init__(
123	            code="idempotency.replayed",
124	            message="Replaying a previously completed idempotent response",
125	            status_code=response_status,
126	        )
127	        self.response_body = response_body

130	@dataclass
131	class IdempotencyContext:
132	    """Yielded to the handler (Phase 2). ``capture`` stages the completion UPDATE on the BUSINESS
133	    session so document + replay record commit atomically; ``captured`` lets the teardown detect a
134	    forgotten capture (fail-closed). ``factory`` + identity are kept so the teardown can run the
135	    separate-session cleanup that deletes the reservation on a forgotten-capture or business
136	    failure."""
137	
138	    session: AsyncSession
139	    factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
140	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
141	    endpoint: str
142	    key: str
143	    captured: bool = False
144	
145	    async def capture[T](self, response: T, *, status_code: int = 200) -> T:
146	        """Write ``UPDATE ... SET status='completed', response_status, response_body,
147	        completed_at=now()`` on the BUSINESS session (no commit) and return ``response``
148	        UNCHANGED. Call it INSIDE the ``run_in_uow`` work, right after the document is created::
149	
150	            async def work() -> None:
151	                doc = create_document(...)
152	                await session.flush()
153	                holder['read'] = await idem.capture(DocRead.model_validate(doc))
154	            await run_in_uow(session, work)
155	            return holder['read']
156	
157	        The UPDATE joins the request's open transaction, so ``run_in_uow``'s single commit persists
158	        the document AND this replay record atomically — they commit or roll back together
159	        (D-013's cardinal invariant: a replayable response exists iff the document exists). The
160	        body is serialized to the exact JSON FastAPI will emit, so a future replay reproduces it
161	        verbatim.
162	
163	        A Core UPDATE under system_context: the reservation is addressed by its full composite PK,
164	        so no tenant filter is needed and bypassing the ORM stamp keeps it a pure data write."""
165	        body = _serialize_response(response)
166	        with system_context():
167	            await self.session.execute(
168	                sa.update(IdempotencyKey.__table__)
169	                .where(
170	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.tenant_id == self.tenant_id,
171	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.endpoint == self.endpoint,
172	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.key == self.key,
173	                )
174	                .values(
175	                    status=STATUS_COMPLETED,
176	                    response_status=status_code,
177	                    response_body=body,
178	                    completed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
179	                )
180	            )
181	        self.captured = True
182	        return response

186	    """Coerce a route's return value (a Pydantic model, a dict, or a primitive) to the
187	    JSON-safe form FastAPI would serialize, so a replay reproduces it byte-for-byte."""
188	    if hasattr(response, "model_dump"):
189	        return response.model_dump(mode="json")

193	async def reserve(
194	    factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession],
195	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
196	    endpoint: str,
197	    key: str,
198	    request_hash: str,
199	) -> None:
200	    """Phase 1 (D-013). Open a SEPARATE session, INSERT the IN_PROGRESS reservation, and COMMIT
201	    immediately so two concurrent duplicates collide on the composite PK. On collision, load the
202	    existing row and decide: replay (raise IdempotencyReplay), key-reuse (422), or in-progress
203	    (409). Runs under system_context so the explicit-tenant_id insert/select bypass ORM stamping
204	    on this out-of-band session; the composite-FK backstop still rejects a bogus tenant_id."""
205	    async with factory() as session:
206	        try:
207	            with system_context():
208	                await session.execute(
209	                    sa.insert(IdempotencyKey.__table__).values(
210	                        tenant_id=tenant_id,
211	                        endpoint=endpoint,
212	                        key=key,
213	                        status=STATUS_IN_PROGRESS,
214	                        request_hash=request_hash,
215	                    )
216	                )
217	                await session.commit()
218	            return
219	        except IntegrityError:
220	            await session.rollback()
221	
222	        # Collision: a row already exists for (tenant, endpoint, key). Load and arbitrate.
223	        with system_context():
224	            existing = (
225	                await session.execute(
226	                    select(IdempotencyKey).where(
227	                        IdempotencyKey.tenant_id == tenant_id,
228	                        IdempotencyKey.endpoint == endpoint,
229	                        IdempotencyKey.key == key,
230	                    )
231	                )
232	            ).scalar_one()

234	    if existing.status == STATUS_COMPLETED:
235	        if existing.request_hash == request_hash:
236	            raise IdempotencyReplay(existing.response_status or 200, existing.response_body)
237	        raise ValidationFailedError(
238	            message="Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request body",
239	            code="idempotency.key_reuse",
240	        )
241	    # IN_PROGRESS: a concurrent duplicate is still running its business work.
242	    raise ConflictError(
243	        message="A request with this Idempotency-Key is already in progress",
244	        code="idempotency.in_progress",
245	    )

270	class Idempotent:
271	    """FastAPI dependency factory (D-013). A guarded route declares it AFTER the principal
272	    dependency (so the D-007 tenant context is set when reserve runs) and captures inside the uow::
273	
274	        @router.post("/journal-entries/{id}/post")
275	        async def post_journal(
276	            current: CurrentUserDep,
277	            session: SessionDep,
278	            idem: IdempotentDep = Depends(Idempotent("finance.journal.post")),
279	        ):
280	            holder = {}
281	            async def work() -> None:
282	                entry = await post_entry(session, ...)        # create the document
283	                holder['read'] = await idem.capture(JournalEntryRead.model_validate(entry))
284	            await run_in_uow(session, work)                   # commits document + replay record
285	            return holder['read']

287	    The ``endpoint`` string is the stable D-013 route identifier (METHOD + template, or a chosen
288	    key) that scopes reservations per endpoint, so one client UUID per form submission is safe."""
289	
290	    def __init__(self, endpoint: str) -> None:
291	        self.endpoint = endpoint
292	
293	    async def __call__(
294	        self,
295	        request: Request,
296	        session: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)],
297	        factory: Annotated[async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], Depends(get_session_factory)],
298	        idempotency_key: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="Idempotency-Key")] = None,
299	    ) -> AsyncIterator[IdempotencyContext]:
300	        if not idempotency_key:
301	            raise ValidationFailedError(
302	                message="The Idempotency-Key header is required for this endpoint",
303	                code="idempotency.key_required",
304	            )
305	        # tenant_id from the D-007 ContextVar that get_current_user set. A guarded route declares
306	        # the principal dependency BEFORE this one (the codebase convention: every router lists
307	        # ``current: CurrentUserDep`` first), so the context is established when reserve() runs. We
308	        # read the ContextVar rather than importing CurrentUserDep here to avoid the deps -> db ->
309	        # idempotency import cycle (this module is registered from core/db at load time).
310	        tenant_id = get_current_tenant_id()
311	        if tenant_id is None:  # pragma: no cover - guarded routes always run authenticated
312	            raise ValidationFailedError(
313	                message="Idempotency requires an active tenant context",
314	                code="idempotency.tenant_required",
315	            )
316	
317	        # Read the raw body here and hash it (D-013). Starlette caches the body on request.body()
318	        # (request._body), so the route handler's own body parsing still works after this read —
319	        # the stream is not consumed out from under it. A replay with a different body therefore
320	        # produces a different hash and is rejected as key-reuse.
321	        request_hash = compute_request_hash(await request.body())
322	        await reserve(factory, tenant_id, self.endpoint, idempotency_key, request_hash)
323	
324	        context = IdempotencyContext(
325	            session=session,
326	            factory=factory,
327	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
328	            endpoint=self.endpoint,
329	            key=idempotency_key,
330	        )
331	        try:
332	            yield context
333	        except Exception:
334	            # Business work failed (D-013 fail-closed): the document was rolled back by run_in_uow
335	            # (the staged capture UPDATE with it), but the IN_PROGRESS reservation was committed in
336	            # reserve()'s SEPARATE session, so it would otherwise linger. Delete it in its own
337	            # committed session so the SAME key is immediately retryable, then re-raise — the app's
338	            # exception handlers turn the re-raised error into the proper envelope (verified: a
339	            # generic Exception still routes through _handle_unexpected_error to a 500 envelope).
340	            await _cleanup_reservation(factory, tenant_id, self.endpoint, idempotency_key)
341	            raise
342	        else:
343	            if not context.captured:
344	                # Forgotten capture: the handler returned 2xx without calling capture(), so the
345	                # reservation never reached COMPLETED. The 2xx response has already been sent (in
346	                # this build the business commit lives in run_in_uow inside the handler, BEFORE
347	                # this teardown — D-013's literal "teardown rolls back" assumed a deferred session
348	                # commit), so the response can no longer be changed. We delete the dangling
349	                # reservation so the key is retryable and log a server error — the missing replay
350	                # record is the signal a guarded route forgot its capture() one-liner. Deviation
351	                # from D-013's rollback-on-forgotten-capture is documented in DECISIONS.md.
352	                await _cleanup_reservation(factory, tenant_id, self.endpoint, idempotency_key)
353	                logger.error(
354	                    "Idempotent endpoint %r returned 2xx without calling capture(); reservation "
355	                    "cleaned up but no replay record was stored",
356	                    self.endpoint,
357	                )
358	
359	
360	# Type alias a guarded route annotates its captured-context parameter with, e.g.
361	# ``idem: IdempotentDep = Depends(Idempotent("finance.journal.post"))``.
362	IdempotentDep = IdempotencyContext
363	
364	__all__ = [
365	    "REPLAYED_HEADER",
366	    "Idempotent",
367	    "IdempotencyContext",
368	    "IdempotencyKey",
369	    "IdempotencyReplay",
370	    "IdempotentDep",
371	    "compute_request_hash",
372	    "reserve",
373	]

65	    The Python ``default``/``onupdate`` fire for ORM and Core inserts alike, so every
66	    stored value uses SQLAlchemy's canonical SQLite string format (six-digit
67	    microseconds). The DDL ``server_default`` remains only as a fallback for raw SQL
68	    outside SQLAlchemy and must never be relied on: SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP writes
69	    second-precision strings whose lexicographic comparison against bound datetimes
70	    breaks keyset-pagination equality — the #34 infinite-page-loop bug."""

73	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),

87	def tenant_fk(target_table: str, local_column: str | None = None) -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
88	    """Tenant-safe foreign key for __table_args__ (D-007 item 4).
89	
90	    - tenant_fk("adm_tenants") anchors tenant_id itself to the tenants root;
91	      every tenant-scoped table carries this backstop.
92	    - tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id") builds the composite (tenant_id, item_id)
93	      -> (inv_items.tenant_id, inv_items.id) FK, so a child row can never point
94	      at a parent row of another tenant; the parent declares tenant_unique().
95	    """
96	    if local_column is None:
97	        return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["tenant_id"], [f"{target_table}.id"])
98	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
99	        ["tenant_id", local_column],
100	        [f"{target_table}.tenant_id", f"{target_table}.id"],
101	    )

107	    constraint starting with tenant_id needs an explicit name at the call site:

1	"""Inventory constants (STRUCTURE §3): enums (UPPER_SNAKE values stored as strings) and the
2	permission keys, registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line
5	cap, the finance precedent); it sits well under that for PLAN 5.1.
6	
7	Item codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_code)`` on
8	inv_items) — mirroring how chart-of-accounts codes work (Account.code is required on create, not
9	auto-numbered). So item/warehouse/bin MASTERS carry no gapless document number (codes, not
10	numbers). Stock MOVES (PLAN 5.2) DO register documents and claim a gapless number — the
11	``inventory.stock_move`` sequence below — because a move is a posted document in the D-012 sense.
12	"""
13	
14	from enum import StrEnum
15	
16	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
17	
18	# Quantity scale (D-015): QuantityType stores scale-6 micro-units. Stock moves and quants use the
19	# same scale; the on-hand>=0 CHECK and the quant sums are exact on both engines.

21	
22	class ItemType(StrEnum):
23	    """What an item IS, which decides whether it carries stock (D-020).
24	
25	    - STOCKED: a physical good tracked in inventory — the only type that participates in stock
26	      moves, costing and lot/serial tracking.
27	    - NON_STOCKED: a purchasable/sellable good NOT held in inventory (e.g. drop-ship, expensed
28	      supplies) — no on-hand quantity, no costing layer.
29	    - SERVICE: a non-physical line item (labour, fees) — never stocked, never tracked.
30	
31	    The service rejects tracking/costing participation for NON_STOCKED/SERVICE so the invariant
32	    "only STOCKED items have stock" holds from the masters up (validated again when moves land)."""
33	
34	    STOCKED = "STOCKED"
35	    NON_STOCKED = "NON_STOCKED"
36	    SERVICE = "SERVICE"
37	
38	
39	class CostingMethod(StrEnum):
40	    """How a stocked item is valued (D-020). Defaulted onto the item FROM its category at create
41	    but STORED on the item, because D-020 changes it only while no stock exists and the item is
42	    the costing unit. The moving-average valuation table and FIFO cost layers arrive in PLAN 5.3;
43	    5.1 only records the method so receipts know which engine to use."""
44	
45	    MOVING_AVERAGE = "MOVING_AVERAGE"
46	    FIFO = "FIFO"
47	
48	
49	class TrackingMode(StrEnum):
50	    """Whether a stocked item's units are individually identified (parity: batch/serial mgmt).
51	
52	    - NONE: fungible — quantity only (the default).
53	    - LOT: grouped by lot/batch code; one lot row per received batch (inv_lots), created at
54	      receipt (5.2+).
55	    - SERIAL: each unit uniquely identified; one inv_serials row per unit, created at receipt.
56	
57	    Tracking is PER ITEM and only meaningful for STOCKED items — the service forbids a non-NONE
58	    mode on NON_STOCKED/SERVICE items."""
59	
60	    NONE = "NONE"
61	    LOT = "LOT"
62	    SERIAL = "SERIAL"
63	
64	
65	class LotStatus(StrEnum):
66	    """Lifecycle of a lot/batch instance (parity: batch management). For 5.1 the table merely
67	    EXISTS — lots are created during receipts (5.2+); AVAILABLE is the default a receipt sets,
68	    the others are reached by later quality/expiry flows. No dead CRUD now (masters-only)."""
69	
70	    AVAILABLE = "AVAILABLE"
71	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
72	    CONSUMED = "CONSUMED"
73	
74	
75	class SerialStatus(StrEnum):
76	    """Lifecycle of a serial-number instance (parity: serial management). Like LotStatus, the
77	    table exists for 5.1 and is populated at receipt (5.2+): IN_STOCK on receipt, ISSUED when
78	    the unit leaves, BLOCKED by quality holds."""
79	
80	    IN_STOCK = "IN_STOCK"
81	    ISSUED = "ISSUED"
82	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
83

85	class MoveType(StrEnum):
86	    """The kind of stock movement (PLAN 5.2). The move's QUANTITY is always positive; the TYPE
87	    decides which of from_bin/to_bin participate (the direction), so a single signed-quantity
88	    column is never needed (the journal one-side-CHECK philosophy applied to stock):
89	
90	    - RECEIPT: stock enters a bin from outside inventory (purchase receipt, opening balance,
91	      positive count adjustment). to_bin REQUIRED, from_bin must be NULL.
92	    - ISSUE: stock leaves a bin to outside inventory (goods issue, scrap, negative count).
93	      from_bin REQUIRED, to_bin must be NULL.
94	    - TRANSFER: stock moves between two bins, conserving total on-hand. BOTH bins REQUIRED and
95	      they must differ.
96	    - ADJUSTMENT: a one-sided correction not tied to a business document. EXACTLY ONE of
97	      from_bin (a decrease) / to_bin (an increase) is set — the side carries the signed intent
98	      while quantity stays positive (a decrease is from_bin-only, an increase is to_bin-only)."""
99	
100	    RECEIPT = "RECEIPT"
101	    ISSUE = "ISSUE"
102	    TRANSFER = "TRANSFER"
103	    ADJUSTMENT = "ADJUSTMENT"

1	"""D-015 exact money/quantity/rate representation on BOTH engines, plus allocation.
2	
3	The financial engine's DB-level invariants (the balance trigger, the one-side CHECK,
4	valuation math) are only meaningful if storage is EXACT on both backends. PostgreSQL has a
5	native NUMERIC; SQLite does not — ``sa.Numeric`` round-trips through float there and silently
6	loses precision. So each TypeDecorator stores NUMERIC on Postgres and an INTEGER of scaled
7	minor units on SQLite (value × 10^scale), converting to/from ``decimal.Decimal`` in the bind/
8	result processors. Trigger SQL therefore only ever SUMs and COMPARES the stored representation
9	(ints on SQLite, NUMERIC on PG) — never divides or scales — so the asymmetric storage stays
10	semantically identical where it matters (D-015 trigger discipline).
11	
12	Scales:
13	- ``MoneyType``      NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — headroom over the
14	  2/3 currency decimals so posting-time rounding has somewhere to live.
15	- ``QuantityType``   NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — UoM/FIFO math.
16	- ``RateType``       NUMERIC(20,10) / INTEGER nano-units (×10^10), scale 10 — FX rates keep
17	  full precision (rates are never quantized to currency decimals).
18	
19	Python is Decimal-only — never float. The TypeDecorators are ``cache_ok = True`` (they carry
20	no per-instance state beyond the fixed class scale), so SQLAlchemy may cache compiled
21	statements that use them.
22	
23	``allocate`` is the single largest-remainder splitter (D-015): tax/discount splits, payment
24	allocation, and the journal's functional-currency residual-cent balancing all route through it
25	so parts always sum EXACTLY to the total. ``quantize_money`` is the ROUND_HALF_UP boundary
26	rounding (commercial/SAP practice), keyed off a per-currency decimal-places lookup.
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
32	
33	import sqlalchemy as sa
34	from sqlalchemy.engine import Dialect
35	from sqlalchemy.types import TypeDecorator
36	
37	# Scales (number of fractional decimal digits each type stores).
38	_MONEY_SCALE = 6
39	_QUANTITY_SCALE = 6
40	_RATE_SCALE = 10
41	
42	
43	class _ScaledDecimalType(TypeDecorator[Decimal]):
44	    """Shared base for the three exact-decimal types (D-015).
45	
46	    ``impl`` is NUMERIC so the default (Postgres) rendering is a true decimal; on SQLite the
47	    column is loaded as INTEGER and the bind/result processors translate Decimal <-> scaled
48	    integer minor units. The conversion is exact in both directions because a Decimal with at
49	    most ``scale`` fractional digits maps to an integer with no rounding (values carrying more
50	    digits than the scale are quantized HALF_UP on the way in — money/quantities are quantized
51	    at their boundary before storage, so this only ever trims trailing noise)."""
52	
53	    # Required by TypeDecorator: the default (Postgres) decorated type. ``load_dialect_impl``
54	    # overrides it per dialect (BigInteger on SQLite, Numeric(precision, scale) on PG).
55	    impl = sa.Numeric
56	    cache_ok = True
57	
58	    # Concrete subclasses set these; the base is abstract by virtue of unset class attrs.
59	    scale: int
60	    precision: int
61	
62	    @property
63	    def python_type(self) -> type[Decimal]:
64	        return Decimal
65	
66	    def load_dialect_impl(self, dialect: Dialect) -> sa.types.TypeEngine[object]:
67	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
68	            # Scaled minor units fit a 64-bit integer for the demo/test value ranges (D-015).
69	            return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.BigInteger())
70	        return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.Numeric(self.precision, self.scale))
71	
72	    @property
73	    def _quantum(self) -> Decimal:
74	        return Decimal(1).scaleb(-self.scale)
75	
76	    def process_bind_param(self, value: Decimal | int | str | None, dialect: Dialect):
77	        if value is None:
78	            return None
79	        as_decimal = value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
80	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
81	            # Decimal -> integer scaled minor units. Quantize first so a value with more than
82	            # ``scale`` digits cannot leave a fractional remainder when multiplied out.
83	            scaled = as_decimal.quantize(self._quantum, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
84	            return int(scaled.scaleb(self.scale))
85	        return as_decimal
86	
87	    def process_result_value(self, value: int | Decimal | None, dialect: Dialect) -> Decimal | None:
88	        if value is None:
89	            return None
90	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
91	            # Integer scaled minor units -> Decimal at the type's scale (exact, no float).
92	            return (Decimal(int(value)) * self._quantum).quantize(self._quantum)
93	        return value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
94	
95	
96	class MoneyType(_ScaledDecimalType):
97	    """Monetary amount (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite."""
98	
99	    # cache_ok must be set on each concrete TypeDecorator class, not just the base.
100	    cache_ok = True
101	    scale = _MONEY_SCALE
102	    precision = 18
103	
104	
105	class QuantityType(_ScaledDecimalType):
106	    """Inventory quantity (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite.
107	    Same storage as MoneyType but a distinct type so quantity and money columns read clearly."""
108	
109	    cache_ok = True
110	    scale = _QUANTITY_SCALE
111	    precision = 18
112	
113	
114	class RateType(_ScaledDecimalType):
115	    """FX/exchange rate (D-015): NUMERIC(20,10) on Postgres, INTEGER nano-units on SQLite.
116	    Scale 10 keeps full rate precision — rates are never quantized to currency decimals."""
117	
118	    cache_ok = True
119	    scale = _RATE_SCALE
120	    precision = 20
121	
122	
123	# --- Currency decimals + boundary rounding ------------------------------------
124	
125	# ISO 4217 fractional digits. Default is 2; non-2-decimal currencies are listed explicitly so
126	# the table can grow (JPY=0, BHD=3, ...). Stored journal amounts quantize to this at the
127	# posting/pricing boundary; unit prices/costs and FX rates keep full scale-6/10 precision.
128	_DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS = 2
129	_CURRENCY_DECIMALS: dict[str, int] = {
130	    "JPY": 0,
131	    "KRW": 0,
132	    "BHD": 3,
133	    "KWD": 3,
134	    "OMR": 3,
135	    "TND": 3,
136	}
137	
138	
139	def currency_decimals(currency_code: str) -> int:
140	    """ISO 4217 fractional digits for ``currency_code`` (default 2). The amount-rounding
141	    boundary uses this so e.g. JPY rounds to whole units and BHD to three places (D-015)."""
142	    return _CURRENCY_DECIMALS.get(currency_code.upper(), _DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS)
143	
144	
145	def quantize_money(value: Decimal, places: int = 2) -> Decimal:
146	    """Round ``value`` to ``places`` decimals HALF_UP (D-015 — commercial/SAP practice). Pass
147	    ``currency_decimals(code)`` for ``places`` to round to a currency's minor unit."""
148	    return value.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
149	
150	
151	def quantize_for_currency(value: Decimal, currency_code: str) -> Decimal:
152	    """Round ``value`` to ``currency_code``'s minor unit HALF_UP (D-015)."""
153	    return quantize_money(value, currency_decimals(currency_code))
154	
155	
156	def allocate(total: Decimal, weights: list[Decimal], places: int = 2) -> list[Decimal]:
157	    """Split ``total`` across ``weights`` so the parts sum EXACTLY to ``total`` (D-015).
158	
159	    Largest-remainder method: each part is ``total × weight / Σweights`` rounded DOWN to
160	    ``places`` decimals, then the rounding residual (``total`` minus the sum of floored parts)
161	    is distributed one minor unit at a time to the parts with the largest fractional remainder,
162	    ties broken by original index. Deterministic, and the parts ALWAYS reconstitute the total —
163	    used for FX residual-cent absorption, tax splits, discount splits and payment allocation.
164	
165	    A zero or empty total returns zeros; zero total weight (all weights zero) splits ``total``
166	    evenly via equal unit weights so the result still sums to ``total`` rather than dropping it.
167	    """
168	    quantum = Decimal(1).scaleb(-places)
169	    n = len(weights)
170	    if n == 0:
171	        return []
172	    total_weight = sum(weights, Decimal(0))
173	    if total_weight == 0:
174	        # Degenerate: no weight to distribute by. Fall back to equal weights so the total is
175	        # still allocated exactly (never silently dropped).
176	        weights = [Decimal(1)] * n
177	        total_weight = Decimal(n)
178	
179	    exact = [total * weight / total_weight for weight in weights]
180	    floored = [part.quantize(quantum, rounding=ROUND_DOWN) for part in exact]
181	    remainders = [exact[i] - floored[i] for i in range(n)]
182	
183	    allocated = sum(floored, Decimal(0))
184	    residual = total - allocated
185	    # Number of whole minor units still to hand out (can be negative if total is negative).
186	    units = int((residual / quantum).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
187	
188	    # Distribute to the largest remainders first; for a negative residual hand out negative
189	    # units to the SMALLEST remainders (those rounded least-down) so the result stays balanced.
190	    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (remainders[i], -i), reverse=units >= 0)
191	    step = quantum if units >= 0 else -quantum
192	    for k in range(abs(units)):
193	        floored[order[k % n]] += step
194	    return floored
195	
196	
197	__all__ = [
198	    "MoneyType",
199	    "QuantityType",
200	    "RateType",
201	    "allocate",
202	    "currency_decimals",
203	    "quantize_for_currency",
204	    "quantize_money",
205	]

1	"""Inventory stock topology + the move ledger + the maintained on-hand projection (PLAN 5.2).
2	
3	This file owns the four STOCK tables (the master tables live in ``models/masters.py``):
4	
5	- ``Warehouse`` / ``Bin``: the storage topology. A bin belongs to a warehouse; on-hand is tracked
6	  PER BIN. Both are reference data (codes, not gapless numbers).
7	- ``StockMove`` (``inv_stock_moves``): the quantity SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (D-020). One append-only
8	  ledger row per movement, POSTED at creation and IMMUTABLE — corrections are reversing moves,
9	  never edits (the universal-journal philosophy of D-017 applied to stock). Quantity is ALWAYS
10	  POSITIVE; the ``move_type`` decides which of from_bin/to_bin participate (the direction), so no
11	  signed column is needed (constants.MOVE_BIN_SIDES). Carries DocumentMixin (registered in
12	  core_documents) and a gapless STK number claimed at creation (D-012 claim-at-permanence — a move
13	  is permanent at create).
14	- ``StockQuant`` (``inv_stock_quants``): the MAINTAINED PROJECTION of the move ledger — current
15	  on-hand per (item, bin, lot). Updated in the SAME transaction as every move (the moving-average
16	  ``inv_item_valuations`` precedent, D-020), so on-hand reads are an indexed point-lookup, not an
17	  unbounded SUM over history (PERFORMANCE §1). The ledger stays the SSOT/audit trail; the quant is
18	  reconcilable from it. A DB ``CHECK (on_hand_qty >= 0)`` plus a pre-flight service check forbid
19	  negative stock outright (D-020) — both engines (a single-column CHECK is portable, D-022).
20	  Recorded as DECISIONS.md D-036.
21	
22	Indexes (PERFORMANCE §1) are declared so the on-hand sums and the move-ledger filters are
23	index-served: moves index (tenant, item, to_bin), (tenant, item, from_bin), (tenant, move_date) and
24	(tenant, item); quants index (tenant, item) on top of the natural-key UNIQUE.
25	
26	Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value (the
27	core/finance/masters convention); the service maps to/from the constants classes. Every table
28	follows the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop (``tenant_unique()`` + ``tenant_fk()`` composites).
29	"""
30	
31	import uuid
32	from datetime import date
33	from decimal import Decimal
34	
35	import sqlalchemy as sa
36	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
37	
38	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
39	from app.core.models import (
40	    AuditMixin,
41	    Base,
42	    TenantMixin,
43	    TimestampMixin,

47	)
48	from app.core.money import MoneyType, QuantityType

51	class Warehouse(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
52	    """A physical or logical stock location grouping bins (parity: plant/storage location).
53	    ``code`` is user-supplied and unique per tenant. ``is_active`` deactivates a warehouse instead
54	    of deleting it (a warehouse referenced by moves/quants must never disappear — the soft-delete
55	    convention). Audited (D-010): topology is master data. ``tenant_unique()`` so bins can reference
56	    it via the composite tenant FK."""
57	
58	    __tablename__ = "inv_warehouses"
59	    __table_args__ = (
60	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_inv_warehouses_tenant_id_code"),
61	        tenant_unique(),
62	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),

65	    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)
66	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
67	    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()

72	class Bin(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
73	    """A storage bin within a warehouse — the granularity on-hand is tracked at (parity: storage
74	    bin). ``warehouse_id`` is a composite tenant FK to inv_warehouses (a bin can never belong to
75	    another tenant's warehouse). ``code`` is unique per (tenant, warehouse) — two warehouses may
76	    both have a bin "A1". ``is_default`` marks the warehouse's default receiving bin (a receipt that
77	    names only a warehouse can resolve to it later); exactly-one-default-per-warehouse is a service
78	    convention, not a DB constraint (a partial unique index is a later optimisation). ``is_active``
79	    deactivates instead of deleting. Audited (D-010)."""

81	    __tablename__ = "inv_bins"
82	    __table_args__ = (
83	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
84	            "tenant_id", "warehouse_id", "code", name="uq_inv_bins_tenant_id_warehouse_id_code"

# --- P2P document status lifecycles (PLAN 6.2) --------------------------------


class RequisitionStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a purchase requisition — the internal "we need to buy this" request.

    - DRAFT: created, editable; lines can change. The PR number is already claimed (D-040).
    - SUBMITTED: handed off for approval. If the estimated total is AT OR ABOVE the active
      REQUISITION approval threshold the requisition STAYS here awaiting an approver; below the
      threshold the submit step auto-advances it to APPROVED (the data-driven rule).
    - APPROVED: cleared to be sourced (→ RFQ) or ordered (→ PO). Terminal-ish until converted.
    - REJECTED: an approver declined it; terminal.
    - CONVERTED: an RFQ or PO was raised from it (source_requisition_id set on the successor);
      terminal — a converted requisition is not edited or re-converted.
    - CANCELLED: abandoned before conversion (from DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED); terminal."""

    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    SUBMITTED = "SUBMITTED"
    APPROVED = "APPROVED"
    REJECTED = "REJECTED"
    CONVERTED = "CONVERTED"
    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"


class RfqStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a request-for-quotation. In v1 an RFQ targets ONE vendor (the vendor being
    asked to quote); multi-bidder comparison is the documented parity later.

    - DRAFT: created, editable.
    - SENT: issued to the vendor (DRAFT→SENT).
    - QUOTED: the vendor's prices have been recorded onto the lines (SENT→QUOTED).
    - CLOSED: sourcing finished (a PO was raised, or the RFQ is shelved); terminal-ish.
    - CANCELLED: abandoned; terminal."""

    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    SENT = "SENT"
    QUOTED = "QUOTED"
    CLOSED = "CLOSED"
    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"


class PurchaseOrderStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a purchase order — the committing P2P document.

    States SET in 6.2: DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED, SENT, CANCELLED.
    States driven by 6.3 GOODS RECEIPTS (declared now as the lifecycle, but the transitions INTO
    them land in 6.3): PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, RECEIVED, CLOSED.

    - DRAFT: created, editable; PO number already claimed (D-040). Lines validated (vendor ACTIVE,
      every item APPROVED for the vendor).
    - PENDING_APPROVAL: a SEND was attempted and the total is AT OR ABOVE the active PURCHASE_ORDER
      approval threshold — awaiting an approver (requires procurement.po.approve).
    - APPROVED: cleared to be sent (below threshold ⇒ the send auto-approves straight to here).
    - REJECTED: an approver declined; terminal.
    - SENT: issued to the vendor — the commitment is live; only an APPROVED PO may be SENT.
    - PARTIALLY_RECEIVED / RECEIVED: set by 6.3 as goods receipts post against the lines
      (received_quantity rises); RECEIVED when every line is fully received.
    - CLOSED: fully received + billed (6.4) or short-closed; terminal.
    - CANCELLED: abandoned before any receipt; terminal (6.3 forbids cancelling a received PO)."""

    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    PENDING_APPROVAL = "PENDING_APPROVAL"
    APPROVED = "APPROVED"
    REJECTED = "REJECTED"
    SENT = "SENT"
    PARTIALLY_RECEIVED = "PARTIALLY_RECEIVED"
    RECEIVED = "RECEIVED"
    CLOSED = "CLOSED"
    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"


class ApprovalDecision(StrEnum):

"""Purchase requisitions (PLAN 6.2): the ``PurchaseRequisition`` header + ``PurchaseRequisitionLine``.

A requisition is the internal "we need to buy this" request — the first document in the P2P chain
(requisition → RFQ → PO). The header mixes in ``DocumentMixin`` (registered in core_documents) and
carries a gapless ``requisition_number`` claimed AT CREATION (D-040 — referenceable immediately).
Lines carry an OPAQUE inventory ``item_id`` (D-029 — a plain ``sa.Uuid``, validated via
``inventory/queries.item_exists``, never a cross-module FK) and an estimated unit cost (the requester
names a budgetary estimate, refined by an RFQ quote or the PO's negotiated price). Money/quantity
columns use ``MoneyType`` / ``QuantityType`` (D-015, exact on both engines).

Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value; the service maps
to/from the constants classes. Every table follows the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop
(``tenant_unique()`` + ``tenant_fk()`` composites + ``document_fk()`` on the header).
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
from app.core.models import (
    AuditMixin,
    Base,
    TenantMixin,
    TimestampMixin,
    UuidPKMixin,
    tenant_fk,
    tenant_unique,
)
from app.core.money import MoneyType, QuantityType
from app.modules.procurement.constants import RequisitionStatus


class PurchaseRequisition(
    UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base
):
    """A purchase requisition header (PLAN 6.2). ``requisition_number`` is the gapless system number
    claimed at creation (D-040; NOT NULL because a requisition is permanent at create — unlike a
    finance bill whose number is NULL until posting). ``status`` runs the RequisitionStatus
    lifecycle; the SUBMIT step evaluates the REQUISITION approval threshold on the estimated total
    (≥ threshold ⇒ stays SUBMITTED awaiting approval, below ⇒ auto APPROVED). ``requested_by`` is the
    requesting user id (opaque, nullable — a requisition may be raised by a system flow). Audited
    (D-010): a document that authorizes spend downstream."""

    __tablename__ = "proc_requisitions"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        document_fk(),
        # The requisition list filters on (tenant, status) and (tenant, requested_by) and sorts by
        # creation (PERFORMANCE §1): composite so the filtered + paginated list is index-served.
        sa.Index("ix_proc_requisitions_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
    )

    requisition_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=RequisitionStatus.DRAFT.value,
        server_default="DRAFT",
    )
    # The requesting user id (opaque core_users id; nullable — a system flow may raise one).
    requested_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    needed_by_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)

An RFQ is the sourcing document — "vendor, what would this cost?". In v1 an RFQ targets ONE vendor

claimed at creation (D-040). An RFQ may be raised FROM an approved requisition
(``source_requisition_id`` set, a nullable composite tenant FK + a docflow edge). Lines copy the
requested item/qty; ``quoted_unit_cost`` (nullable ``MoneyType``) is filled when the vendor's prices
are recorded (the SENT→QUOTED step).

Enum columns are plain ``sa.String``; every table follows the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop.
